full_text: Trimsamsa (D30): Each sign divided into 5 unequal parts totaling 30°. For ODD signs: Mars rules 0°-5° (5°); Saturn rules 5°-10° (5°); Jupiter rules 10°-18° (8°); Mercury rules 18°-25° (7°); Venus rules 25°-30° (5°). For EVEN signs: BOTH planet order AND degree widths are reversed — CONFIRMED (TT-CH06-01 resolved 2026-05-31): Venus rules 0°-5° (5°); Mercury rules 5°-12° (7°); Jupiter rules 12°-20° (8°); Saturn rules 20°-25° (5°); Mars rules 25°-30° (5°). Sun and Moon have no Trimsamsa. Used for assessment of evil acts and adversity.

condition.subject: Trimsamsa_D30
condition.description: Trimsamsa (D30) computation: 5 unequal divisions (5°+5°+8°+7°+5°) ruled by Mars/Saturn/Jupiter/Mercury/Venus for odd signs; reversed for even

claim.text: Trimsamsa D30: Unequal divisions. Odd signs: Mars(0-5°/5°), Saturn(5-10°/5°), Jupiter(10-18°/8°), Mercury(18-25°/7°), Venus(25-30°/5°). Even signs — BOTH order AND widths reversed: Venus(0-5°/5°), Mercury(5-12°/7°), Jupiter(12-20°/8°), Saturn(20-25°/5°), Mars(25-30°/5°). Interpretation (b) confirmed: the reversal applies to BOTH the planetary sequence and the degree extents simultaneously. Sun/Moon have no Trimsamsa. Used for general life assessment and evil/sinful acts.

decode_notes: TT-CH06-01 ✅ RESOLVED 2026-05-31: Even-sign = BOTH order AND widths reversed (interpretation b confirmed).

full_text: Chatvarimsamsa / Khavedamsa (D40): Each sign divided into 40 equal parts of 45' each. For ODD signs: 40 Khavedamsas distributed from Aries. For EVEN signs: from Libra. Presiding deities repeat in same order for all signs: Vishnu, Chandra, Marichi, Tvashta, Dhata, Siva, Ravi, Yama, Yaksha, Gandhara, Kala, Varuna (repeating successively; in the 4th round only up to Tvashta).

condition.subject: Khavedamsa_D40
condition.description: Khavedamsa/Chatvarimsamsa (D40) computation: odd from Aries; even from Libra

claim.text: Khavedamsa D40 (Chatvarimsamsa): Size=45' per division. Odd sign: from Aries. Even sign: from Libra. 40 consecutive divisions. Used for auspicious/inauspicious results in general.

full_text: Akshavedamsa (D45): Each sign divided into 45 equal parts of 40' each. For MOVABLE signs: from Aries. For FIXED (immovable) signs: from Leo. For DUAL/COMMON signs: from Sagittarius. In movable signs: Brahma, Siva, Vishnu repeat 15 times. In fixed signs: Siva, Vishnu, Brahma repeat 15 times. In dual signs: Vishnu, Brahma, Siva repeat 15 times.

condition.subject: Akshavedamsa_D45
condition.description: Akshavedamsa (D45) computation: movable from Aries; fixed from Leo; dual from Sagittarius

full_text: Shashtiamsa (D60): Each sign divided into 60 equal parts of 30' each. Computation method: Ignore the sign position of the planet; take the degrees + minutes it has traversed in that sign. Multiply that by 2. Divide the degrees by 12; add 1 to the remainder. Count that many signs from the planet's sign. The resulting sign is the Shashtiamsa position, and its lord is the Shashtiamsa lord. In ODD signs: 60 named Shashtiamsas from Ghora to Chandrarekha. In EVEN signs: the same 60 names in REVERSE order.

condition.subject: Shashtiamsa_D60
condition.description: Shashtiamsa (D60) computation: degree-based formula (degree × 2 ÷ 12, remainder + 1 = sign count from planet's sign)

claim.text: Shashtiamsa D60: Size=30' per division. Formula: (planet degrees in sign × 2) ÷ 12 → remainder + 1 = count from planet's sign → gives Shashtiamsa sign. Even sign: reverse name order. The most important Varga for overall life quality. Planets in benefic Shashtiamsas produce auspicious results; malefic = inauspicious.

full_text: Four Varga classification systems: (1) Shadvarga (6 Vargas): Rasi + Hora + Drekkana + Navamsa + Dvadasamsa + Trimsamsa. (2) Saptavarga (7 Vargas): Shadvarga + Saptamamsa. (3) Dasavarga (10 Vargas): Saptavarga + Shodasamsa + Dasamsa + Shashtiamsa. (4) Shodasavarga (16 Vargas): All 16 divisions.

condition.subject: Varga_groupings
condition.description: Four standard Varga grouping systems from Shadvarga to full Shodasavarga

claim.text: Varga systems: Shadvarga=D1+D2+D3+D9+D12+D30 (6 divisions). Saptavarga=Shadvarga+D7. Dasavarga=Saptavarga+D16+D10+D60. Shodasavarga=all 16 divisions. Each system gives progressively more refined planetary strength assessment.

full_text: Good Varga criteria: A Varga division is counted as 'good' (auspicious) for a planet if the planet is in: (1) Its exaltation division, (2) Its Moolatrikona division, (3) Its own sign division, or (4) A division belonging to the lord of an angle from the Arudha Pada/Pada Lagna.

condition.subject: good_varga
condition.description: Four criteria for classifying a Varga division as 'good' for a planet

claim.text: A Varga is 'good' if planet is in: exaltation sign's division, Moolatrikona division, own sign division, or division ruled by a lord of angles from Arudha Pada. Count of good Vargas across the applicable Varga system gives the Varga classification name.

full_text: Varga classification destroyers: The divisions of a combust planet, a defeated planet (in planetary war), a weak planet, or a planet in a bad Avastha (like Sayana/sleeping) are all to be ignored as auspicious. These conditions destroy the good Yoga indicated by Varga positions.

condition.subject: planet
condition.description: Conditions that nullify good Varga designations: combustion, defeat, weakness, bad Avastha

claim.text: Good Varga counts are void/ignored for: combust planets (near Sun), planets defeated in planetary war, weak planets (insufficient Shadbala), planets in bad Avasthas (Sayana etc.). These planetary states destroy the good Yoga otherwise indicated by Varga strength.

full_text: Shadvarga designation names: A planet having good Vargas in the Shadvarga (Rasi+Hora+Drekkana+Navamsa+Dvadasamsa+Trimsamsa) receives a designation based on count of good Vargas: 2 good = Kimsuka; 3 good = Vyanjana; 4 good = Chamara; 5 good = Chatra; 6 good = Kundala.

condition.subject: Shadvarga_designations
condition.description: Shadvarga (6-Varga system) designation names by count of good Vargas

claim.text: Shadvarga: 2 good = Kimsuka (modest results); 3 good = Vyanjana (good results); 4 good = Chamara (very good); 5 good = Chatra (excellent); 6 good = Kundala (outstanding planet). Designation conveys overall planetary dignity and expected quality of results.

full_text: Saptavarga designation: The Saptavarga (Shadvarga + Saptamamsa) adds one additional designation at the top: 7 good Vargas = Mukuta (crown). This is the highest designation in the 7-Varga system. The six lower designations (Kimsuka through Kundala) carry forward from Shadvarga.

condition.subject: Saptavarga_designations
condition.description: Saptavarga system: 6 Shadvarga names + Mukuta at 7 good Vargas

claim.text: Saptavarga adds Mukuta (crown) designation at 7 good Vargas (all 7 divisions). A planet with Mukuta designation in Saptavarga is of exceptional power and dignity.

full_text: Dasavarga designation names: The Dasavarga (Saptavarga + Shodasamsa + Dasamsa + Shashtiamsa = 10 Vargas) has 9 designations for 2-10 good Vargas: 2 good = Parijata; 3 = Uttama; 4 = Gopura; 5 = Simhasana (lion throne); 6 = Paravata; 7 = Devaloka; 8 = Brahmaloka; 9 = Sakravahana; 10 = Sridhama.

full_text: Hora Varga exception for good count: For the Hora Varga specifically, the conditions for a 'good' Hora division differ by planet. Sun, Jupiter and Mars are good in the Sun's Hora (Leo's Hora). Mercury alone is good in BOTH Horas. All other planets (Moon, Venus, Saturn, Rahu, Ketu) are good in the Moon's Hora (Cancer's Hora). This exception applies only to the Hora within any Varga classification scheme.

condition.subject: Hora_good_varga_exception
condition.description: Special rule for which planets count the Hora as a 'good' Varga: Sun-group in Sun Hora; Moon-group in Moon Hora; Mercury in both

claim.text: Hora good-Varga exceptions: Sun/Jupiter/Mars → Sun's Hora is their 'good' Hora. Moon/Venus/Saturn/Rahu/Ketu → Moon's Hora is their 'good' Hora. Mercury → BOTH Horas are good. This is the sole exception to the standard four good-Varga criteria.

full_text: Trimsamsa exception for Sun and Moon: The Sun and the Moon do not have any Trimsamsa (D30) divisions of their own. Therefore neither planet can ever be counted as having a 'good' Trimsamsa for purposes of Varga classification. When computing Shadvarga, Dasavarga, or Shodasavarga good-Varga counts for the Sun or Moon, the Trimsamsa count is automatically excluded.

condition.subject: Trimsamsa_Sun_Moon_exception
condition.description: Sun and Moon have no Trimsamsa lordship; their good-Varga count excludes Trimsamsa

claim.text: Sun and Moon cannot gain a 'good' Trimsamsa Varga. Trimsamsa is excluded from good-Varga count for both luminaries in all Varga classification computations (Shadvarga/Dasavarga/Shodasavarga). The Trimsamsa is wholly governed by Mars/Saturn/Jupiter/Mercury/Venus.

For each of the 12 bhavas, its own Varnada can be computed. The Bhava Varnada Dasa for each bhava equals one-twelfth (1/12) of the main Varnada Dasa period. The direction (clockwise or anti-clockwise) follows the same rule as for the natal ascendant Varnada.

full_text: Ch05 tail (slokas 23-24): The natal ascendant (Janma Lagna) is calculated based on the birth PLACE — it is location-specific. By contrast, Bhava Lagna, Hora Lagna, and Ghatika Lagna are NOT birthplace-specific — they are common to all places on the earth for a native born at the same point in time. These three special lagnas depend only on the time of birth (ghatis from sunrise) and the Sun's position, both of which are universal.

Benefic Shashtiamsas like Kubera, Deva, Amrita, Indu, Brahma, Vishnu, Maheswara indicate auspicious life outcomes in the areas governed by the planet and house involved.

full_text: Shashtiamsa predictive application example 2: A planet posited in the 8th house in the Payodhi Shashtiamsa (D60 division #58 — Payodhi = ocean) indicates fear from or danger involving water for the native. full_text: Use of the 16 Divisional Charts (Shodasavargas): Each of the 16 Vargas is the primary instrument for a specific life domain. Ascendant/Rasi = physique; Hora(D2) = wealth; Drekkana(D3) = happiness through co-born; Chaturthamsa(D4) = fortune/property; Saptamamsa(D7) = sons/progeny dynasty; Navamsa(D9) = spouse; Dasamsa(D10) = power and position/livelihood; Dvadasamsa(D12) = parents; Shodasamsa/Kalamsa(D16) = vehicles and conveyances; Vimsamsa(D20) = worship and spiritual progress; Chaturvimsamsa/Siddhamsa(D24) = academic achievements; Bhamsa/Nakshatramsa(D27) = strength and weakness; Trimsamsa(D30) = evil effects; Khavedamsa(D40) = auspicious and inauspicious effects; Akshavedamsa(D45) = all general indications; Shashtiamsa(D60) = all general indications.

Assessment of each domain requires its primary Varga.

full_text: Bhava flourish/diminish via Shashtiamsa and Kalamsa: The bhava whose lord is in a MALEFIC Shashtiamsa (D60) will diminish in its indications — so say Garga and others. The bhava whose lord is in a BENEFIC Shodasamsa (Kalamsa, D16) will flourish. Here 'benefic' and 'malefic' refer to the named Shashtiamsa/Kalamsa divisions themselves, not to planet dignity.

full_text: Chaturvimsamsa (D24) for education: Taking the 2nd and 4th lords in the Chaturvimsamsa (Siddhamsa) as the example — if these lords occupy favourable Chaturvimsamsa positions, the native will progress with education unhindered. If the Dasa lord related to education is also dignified in Chaturvimsamsa, wide learning is conferred. Similarly, other events must be assessed through their respective primary Vargas.

full_text: Bhava malefic Shashtiamsa rule (clarification): If a planet is in a malefic Shashtiamsa, then the bhava OWNED BY that planet suffers a defect. This is distinct from the planet being placed in a malefic house — it is specifically about the planet's Shashtiamsa position affecting its owned bhavas.

full_text: Vimsopaka Strength — definition and basis: Vimsopaka is the 20-point strength derived by assessing a planet's placement in the Varga divisions of any of the four Varga schemes (Shadvarga, Saptavarga, Dasavarga or Shodasavarga). A planet continuously occupying its own Vargas in the whole scheme gets full 20 points. Knowing the Vimsopaka strength, the results of this birth and former births clearly emerge.

condition.subject: Vimsopaka
condition.description: Vimsopaka = 20-point Varga strength system. Core definition and application.

claim.text: Vimsopaka = 20-point scale of planetary strength derived from Varga occupancy. Full 20 = planet in own Vargas across entire scheme. Used to assess quality of results during Dasa periods. Applicable to any of the 4 Varga schemes.

full_text: Vimsopaka — exaltation and debilitation strength rule: A planet in exaltation is fully powerful (maximum Vimsopaka strength for that Varga). In debilitation, it is bereft of vigour (zero effective strength for that Varga). If a planet is descending (leaving exaltation and approaching debilitation), its strength diminishes degree by degree and is fully void at the debilitation sign. If ascending (climbing from debilitation toward exaltation), strength gradually increases to full potential.

condition.subject: planet
condition.description: Exaltation = full Vimsopaka; debilitation = zero. Proportional gradient in between.

claim.text: Exaltation = full Vimsopaka strength. Debilitation = zero. Descending (post-exaltation toward debilitation): strength decreases proportionally. Ascending (post-debilitation toward exaltation): strength increases proportionally. Rule applies within each Varga division.

full_text: Vimsopaka — own sign full strength, with gender rule: Planets in their own signs get full strength. Additionally, male planets in male signs and female planets in female signs get full strength. Mars, a male planet, in own sign Aries (male) is better than Mars in Scorpio (female sign). Venus in Taurus (female sign) is better placed than Venus in Libra (male sign). These distinctions apply in Varga calculations.

condition.subject: planet
condition.description: Planet in own sign = full Vimsopaka; gender-sign congruence enhances strength

claim.text: Own sign = full Vimsopaka strength. Gender congruence enhances: male planet in male sign > male planet in female sign. Female planet in female sign > in male sign. Both criteria apply in Varga strength evaluation. Male signs: Aries/Gemini/Leo/Libra/Sagittarius/Aquarius. Female: Taurus/Cancer/Virgo/Scorpio/Capricorn/Pisces.

full_text: Hora, Drekkana and Trimsamsa planetary efficacy rules: Jupiter, Sun and Mars give pronounced effects in the Sun's Hora. Moon, Venus and Saturn give pronounced effects in the Moon's Hora. Mercury is effective in both Horas. In an even Rasi, the Moon's Hora is powerful; in an odd Rasi, the Sun's Hora is powerful. Effects are FULL in the first one-third of a Hora, MEDIUM in the middle third, and NIL in the last third. Similar applications for Drekkana, Turyamsa (D4), Navamsa. For Trimsamsa: Sun is akin to Mars; Moon is akin to Venus (in terms of Trimsamsa effects).

claim.text: Hora efficacy: Sun/Jupiter/Mars in Sun's Hora = full; Moon/Venus/Saturn in Moon's Hora = full; Mercury in both = effective. Position within Hora: first 1/3 = full effects, middle 1/3 = medium, last 1/3 = nil. Even sign: Moon's Hora dominant; Odd sign: Sun's Hora dominant. Applies similarly to Drekkana and D4. Trimsamsa: Sun treated as Mars-equivalent, Moon as Venus-equivalent.

full_text: Vimsopaka computation formula: Net Vimsopaka strength = (Swaviswa × Varga Viswa) ÷ 20. Where Swaviswa = the full-point value allotted to that Varga in the scheme (from the tables), and Varga Viswa = the relationship-based score (Own=20, extreme friend=18, friend=15, equal=10, enemy=7, extreme enemy=5). This formula is applied for each Varga in the scheme and the results are summed for total Vimsopaka.

full_text: Vimsopaka result thresholds (4-grade): Below 5 = inauspicious (planet incapable of giving good results / neutralises good effects). 5 to 10 = planet yields some good effects. 10 to 15 = mediocre/indicative effects. Above 15 = wholly favourable effects. These thresholds apply to the total net Vimsopaka score in whichever Varga scheme is being used.

full_text: Vimsopaka 8-grade classification table (Atipoorna to Atheena): The Vimsopaka strength during a Dasa period is classified as: Atipoorna (17.5-20.0 pts = 87.5-100% beneficial effects); Poorna (15.0-17.5 = 75-87.5%); Atimadhya (12.5-15.0 = 62.5-75%); Madhya (10.0-12.5 = 50-62.5%); Swalpa (7.5-10.0 = 37.5-50%); Atiswalpa (5.0-7.5 = 25-37.5%); Heena (2.5-5.0 = 12.5-25%); Atheena (0-2.5 = 0-12.5%). Dasa results are declared according to these grades.

full_text: Sun's 7th — full planetary efficacy; combustion destroys: Planets in the 7th from the Sun will be fully effective. A planet with identical longitude to the Sun destroys its good effects. The rule of three process is applied to assess planets located between the 7th-from-Sun position and the Sun itself. A combust planet proves impotent (eclipsed and unable to give results). Rahu and Ketu are not treated as combust even if longitudinally close to the Sun — they are mathematical points that eclipse the Sun, not the reverse.

condition.subject: planet
condition.description: 7th-from-Sun = fully effective; same longitude as Sun = destroyed; Rahu/Ketu not combust

claim.text: Planet in 7th from Sun = fully effective. Planet at same longitude as Sun = good effects destroyed (combust). Between these extremes: rule of three interpolation. Rahu and Ketu are NOT combust near Sun. Applies to Venus and Saturn as well — they also lose rays in combustion despite common belief otherwise.

full_text: Combustion degree thresholds: Moon combust within 12° of Sun; Mars within 17° (retrograde 8°); Mercury within 14° (retrograde 12°); Jupiter within 11° (retrograde 11°); Venus within 10° (retrograde 8°); Saturn within 16° (retrograde 16°). A planet heliacally set (invisible due to solar proximity) during its combustion period cannot give results in that period.

condition.subject: combustion_degrees

claim.text: Combustion thresholds (direct/retrograde): Moon=12°/n.a., Mars=17°/8°, Mercury=14°/12°, Jupiter=11°/11°, Venus=10°/8°, Saturn=16°/16°. Within these distances from Sun: planet combust → heliacally set → impotent. Rahu/Ketu excluded from combustion.

full_text: House group classifications (Bhava categories): Kendras (angles) = 1st, 4th, 7th, 10th. Panapharas (succedents) = 2nd, 5th, 8th, 11th. Apoklimas (cadents) = 3rd, 6th, 9th, 12th. Konas (trines) = 5th, 9th (from ascendant). Trikas (evil/malefic houses) = 6th, 8th, 12th. Chaturasras = 4th, 8th. Upachayas (growing houses) = 3rd, 6th, 10th, 11th.

full_text: Indications from houses via co-signifying planets: The primary co-significators for each bhava domain — Father: 9th from ASC and 9th from Sun both must be assessed; also 10th and 11th from ASC correlate with 10th and 11th from Sun for paternal matters. Mother: 4th from ASC and 4th from Moon; also 1st, 2nd, 11th from Moon. Co-borns/younger siblings: 3rd from ASC and 3rd from Mars. Disease/debts/enemies: 6th from ASC and 6th from Mercury. Progeny: 5th from ASC and 5th from Jupiter. Spouse: 7th from ASC and 7th from Venus. Death/longevity: 8th and 12th from ASC with 8th and 12th from Saturn. Gains: 11th from ASC and from Moon and from Sun.

condition.subject: bhava_co_significators
condition.description: Co-signifying planet rule: each bhava domain must be assessed both from ascendant and from the natural significator of that domain

claim.text: Every bhava must be assessed from TWO sources: (1) the relevant house from natal ascendant, and (2) the same house from the natural significator planet. Father=9th from ASC+Sun. Mother=4th from ASC+Moon. Siblings=3rd from ASC+Mars. Enemies/debts=6th from ASC+Mercury. Children=5th from ASC+Jupiter. Spouse=7th from ASC+Venus. Death=8th/12th from ASC+Saturn. Both must be strong for positive results.

full_text: Bhava lord equally important rule: The lord of the bhava is equally important when estimating the indications of a particular bhava (house). It is not sufficient for the house counted from the ascendant to be strong — the bhava lord must also be strong. If the natural significator's position (e.g., 9th from Sun for father) is adversely occupied, it neutralises good indicators from the natal ascendant chart.

condition.subject: bhava_lord

claim.text: Bhava analysis requires both: (1) the bhava house strength itself, and (2) the bhava lord's strength and placement. Strong bhava + weak lord → partial results. If natural significator house is also afflicted (e.g., 9th from Sun for father is debilitated), good natal chart indicators for that bhava are neutralised.

full_text: Rasi (sign) aspects — movable sign rule: Every movable sign aspects the 3 fixed signs, LEAVING (not aspecting) the fixed sign adjacent to it. Movable signs are: Aries, Cancer, Leo, Libra. Wait — movable = Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn. Fixed = Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius. The adjacent fixed sign (the one immediately next in zodiacal order) is excluded. Example: Aries (movable) → does NOT aspect Taurus (adjacent fixed), but DOES aspect Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius.

condition.subject: movable_sign
condition.description: Movable sign Rasi aspect rule: aspects 3 of the 4 fixed signs, skipping the immediately adjacent one

claim.text: Rasi aspect — movable signs: Aries→Leo/Scorpio/Aquarius; Cancer→Scorpio/Aquarius/Taurus; Libra→Aquarius/Taurus/Leo; Capricorn→Taurus/Leo/Scorpio. Each movable sign skips the fixed sign immediately next to it in the zodiac.

full_text: Rasi aspects — fixed sign rule: Every fixed sign lends aspect to 3 movable signs, BARRING (not aspecting) the adjacent movable sign. Fixed signs: Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius. Example: Taurus (fixed) → does NOT aspect Aries (the adjacent movable sign immediately preceding it), but DOES aspect Cancer, Libra, Capricorn.

condition.subject: fixed_sign
condition.description: Fixed sign Rasi aspect rule: aspects 3 of the 4 movable signs, skipping the immediately adjacent one

claim.text: Rasi aspect — fixed signs: Taurus→Cancer/Libra/Capricorn; Leo→Libra/Capricorn/Aries; Scorpio→Capricorn/Aries/Cancer; Aquarius→Aries/Cancer/Libra. Each fixed sign skips the movable sign immediately preceding it in the zodiac.

full_text: Rasi aspects — dual/common sign rule: A dual (common/mutable) sign aspects ALL three other dual signs. Dual signs: Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces. Each dual sign aspects all three of the remaining dual signs — no exclusion. Gemini aspects Virgo, Sagittarius and Pisces; Virgo aspects Gemini, Sagittarius and Pisces; Sagittarius aspects Gemini, Virgo and Pisces; Pisces aspects Gemini, Virgo and Sagittarius.

condition.subject: dual_sign
condition.description: Dual/common sign Rasi aspect rule: aspects all other 3 dual signs — no exclusion

claim.text: Rasi aspect — dual signs: Gemini↔Virgo↔Sagittarius↔Pisces — all four dual signs mutually aspect each other (each aspects the other three). No exclusion rule applies to dual signs, unlike movable and fixed.

full_text: Planet inherits sign aspect: The planet in a sign lends the same aspect as the sign (in which the planet is) does. Rasi aspects are sign-to-sign and planet-to-sign, NOT degree-to-degree. Longitude of the aspector and the aspected are irrelevant — only sign placement matters. This system is distinct from the conventional degree-based Graha Drishti planetary aspects.

condition.subject: planet
condition.description: Planetary Rasi aspect = same as the sign's aspect. Longitude-independent.

claim.text: A planet aspects all signs aspected by its sign. Rasi aspects are degree-independent — only the sign occupied by the planet determines which signs and occupants it aspects. This is the Parashari Rasi Drishti system (also used in Jaimini). It is separate from Graha Drishti (degree-based planetary aspects).

full_text: Rasi aspects are bidirectional (mutual): When a sign aspects another sign, the planet in the aspected sign is ALSO subjected to the aspect — the aspect acts in both directions simultaneously. If sign A aspects sign B, then a planet in B receives A's aspect AND aspects back to A (and A's occupant). All Rasi aspects are inherently mutual.

condition.subject: rasi_aspect
condition.description: Rasi aspects are mutual/bidirectional: both signs and their occupants aspect each other

claim.text: Rasi aspects are mutual. If sign/planet A aspects sign/planet B, then B simultaneously aspects A. No unidirectional Rasi aspects exist. Planet in aspected sign receives AND returns the aspect. This makes Rasi Drishti relationships symmetrical, unlike conventional Graha Drishti which can be unidirectional.

full_text: Rasi aspects also aspect occupants: A planet in a sign that aspects another sign also aspects the PLANETS occupying that aspected sign. Similarly the occupants of the aspected sign cast their sign's aspect back. The aspect is both sign-to-sign and occupant-to-occupant simultaneously.

condition.subject: rasi_aspect_occupants

claim.text: Planet in sign X aspects: (1) sign Y (the aspected sign), and (2) all planets occupying sign Y. This means a planet receives Rasi aspects from all planets occupying signs that aspect the planet's sign. Useful for yoga formation, malefic/benefic influence assessment, and Jaimini-style analysis.

full_text: Aspectual diagram — directional sign placement: Lord Brahma's aspectual diagram maps the 12 signs to the 8 compass directions. Aries and Taurus = East; Gemini = North-East; Cancer and Leo = North; Virgo = North-West; Libra and Scorpio = West; Sagittarius = South-West; Capricorn and Aquarius = South; Pisces = South-East. The aspect connections between signs (per slokas 1-5) can then be visualised as lines on this directional square or circle.

full_text: The life span of the child will be either 2 months or 6 months only, if all planets devoid of strength are relegated to Apoklima houses (i.e. 3rd, 6th, 9th and 12th).

condition.subject: all_planets
condition.additional: All planets in Apoklima houses (3/6/9/12) AND all planets devoid of strength

claim.text: All planets in Apoklimas (3rd/6th/9th/12th) AND all weak → life of only 2 months or 6 months. No Kendra or Panaphara occupation at all combined with universal weakness = extreme Balarishta.

full_text: EVILS TO MOTHER (slokas 24-33): The mother of the native will incur evils (will die soon) if the Moon at birth is aspected by three malefics. Benefics aspecting the Moon will bring good to the mother.

condition.subject: Moon
condition.additional: Moon aspected by 3 malefics simultaneously

claim.text: Moon aspected by 3 malefics at birth → mother will die soon after child's birth. Benefics aspecting Moon → good outcomes for mother. Applicable to assessment of mother's longevity from the natal chart.

full_text: Should the 2nd house be occupied by Rahu, Mercury, Venus, Sun and Saturn, the child's birth has been after its father's death while even the mother will face early death.

condition.subject: 2nd_house
condition.additional: All five in 2nd house

claim.text: Rahu + Mercury + Venus + Sun + Saturn all in 2nd house → (a) child born after father's death (posthumous birth), AND (b) mother also faces early death.

full_text: If the Moon is in the 7th or 8th from a malefic, be herself with a malefic, and be aspected by a strong malefic — predict mother's end to be early.

condition.subject: Moon
condition.additional: Moon in 7th/8th from a malefic + Moon conjunct a malefic + Moon aspected by strong malefic (triple malefic involvement)

claim.text: Moon in 7th or 8th from a malefic + Moon conjunct another malefic + Moon aspected by a strong malefic → mother's early death. Three simultaneous malefic connections to Moon = strong indicator.

full_text: The child will not live on mother's milk but on that of a she-goat if the Sun is exalted or debilitated in the 7th. Notes: For Aries native, Sun debilitated in 7th (Libra); for Libra, Sun exalted in 7th (Aries) — both deprive mother's milk (7th rules 4th via being 4th from 4th). Saturn in the 4th will also deprive one of mother's milk. Atmakaraka in Scorpio Navamsa produces similar effects.

condition.subject: Sun
condition.additional: Sun exalted OR debilitated in 7th

claim.text: Sun exalted or debilitated in 7th → child deprived of mother's milk (nurturing by mother). Saturn in 4th → same result. Atmakaraka in Scorpio Navamsa → similar effect. 7th governs 4th from 4th (nursing/nourishment from mother).

full_text: Should a malefic be in the 4th, identical with an inimical sign (counted from the Moon), while there is no benefic in an angle, the child will lose its mother in a premature manner.

condition.subject: malefic
condition.additional: Malefic in 4th in an inimical sign (counted from Moon) + no benefic in Kendra

claim.text: Malefic in 4th in a sign inimical to it (counted from Moon's position) + no benefic in any angular house → premature loss of mother.

full_text: Malefics in the 6th and 12th will bring evils to mother. The child's father will receive similar effects if the 4th and 10th are captured by malefics.

condition.subject: malefic
condition.additional: Malefics in 6th AND 12th simultaneously

claim.text: Malefics in 6th + 12th → evil/harm to mother. Same pattern applied to 4th + 10th → evil/harm to father. The 6-12 axis affliction → mother; 4-10 axis affliction → father.

full_text: Mercury in the 2nd while malefics occupy the ascendant, 7th and 12th — this yoga will destroy the entire family.

condition.subject: Mercury
condition.additional: Mercury in 2nd + malefics in ASC + malefics in 7th + malefics in 12th

claim.text: Mercury in 2nd + malefics in ASC + 7th + 12th → destruction of the entire family (Kula nasa yoga). The 2nd house (family lineage) afflicted via Mercury surrounded by malefics on three sides.

full_text: Jupiter, Saturn and Rahu respectively posited in the ascendant, 2nd and 3rd will cause mother's death early.

condition.subject: multiple
condition.additional: Jupiter in ASC, Saturn in 2nd, Rahu in 3rd

claim.text: Jupiter in ASC + Saturn in 2nd + Rahu in 3rd → mother's early death. Despite Jupiter in ASC (normally protective), Saturn+Rahu in 2nd+3rd overwhelm the benefic protection for the mother.

full_text: Doubtlessly the mother will give up the child if it has malefics in trines counted from the decreasing Moon — no benefic shall be in conjunction with the said malefics.

condition.subject: malefic
condition.additional: Malefics in trines (5th and 9th) from waning Moon + no benefic conjunct those malefics

claim.text: Malefics in 5th and/or 9th from decreasing (waning) Moon + no benefic conjunct them → mother abandons the child. Combined with waning Moon's weakness, trine malefics destroy the 5th (progeny) and 9th (father/fortune) from the Moon's perspective.

full_text: If Mars and Saturn are together in an angle with reference to the Moon and occupy one and the same Navamsa, the child will have two mothers. Yet it will be short-lived.

condition.subject: Mars_Saturn
condition.additional: Mars+Saturn conjunct in a Kendra from Moon AND in the same Navamsa sign

claim.text: Mars + Saturn together in angular house from Moon + in same Navamsa division → native has two mothers (step-mother or adoption). Short life despite the two-mother indication. D9 confirmation of the yoga required (same Navamsa).

full_text: EVILS TO FATHER (slokas 34-42): One's father will incur early death if Saturn, Mars and the Moon are in their order in the ascendant, the 7th and the 6th.

condition.subject: multiple
condition.additional: Saturn in ASC, Mars in 7th, Moon in 6th

claim.text: Saturn in ASC + Mars in 7th + Moon in 6th → father's early death. The 9th house (father) is afflicted by this pattern through the lords/significators.

full_text: The native will at the time of his marriage lose his father if Jupiter is in the ascendant while Saturn, Sun, Mars and Mercury are together in the 2nd.

condition.subject: multiple
condition.additional: Jupiter in ASC + Saturn+Sun+Mars+Mercury all in 2nd

claim.text: Jupiter in ASC + Saturn+Sun+Mars+Mercury all together in 2nd → father dies at time of native's marriage. Timing marker: marriage period activates this yoga.

full_text: Early loss of father will take place if the Sun is with a malefic or is hemmed between malefics as there is another malefic in the 7th from the Sun.

condition.subject: Sun
condition.additional: Sun with malefic OR Sun hemmed between malefics (Papakartari on Sun) + malefic in 7th from Sun

claim.text: Sun conjunct malefic (or Papakartari on Sun) + malefic in 7th from Sun → early loss of father. The Sun is the natural significator of father; affliction from both sides (Kartari + opposite house) indicates paternal loss.

full_text: Remote will be the possibility of one's father sustaining if the Sun is in the 7th while Mars is in the 10th and Rahu is in the 12th.

claim.text: Sun in 7th + Mars in 10th + Rahu in 12th → father's death highly likely (remote chance of father surviving). Sun (father significator) in 7th (12th from 8th), Mars in 10th, Rahu in 12th creates severe paternal affliction.

full_text: Early and doubtless will be one's father's death if Mars is in the 10th identical with his enemy's sign. Mercury is the sole enemy of Mars (vide Ch.3, verse 55). Mercury's signs are Gemini and Virgo. Hence for a Sagittarius native or for a Virgo native, Mars in the 10th (in Gemini or Virgo respectively) will cause early death of father.

condition.subject: Mars
condition.additional: Mars in 10th in an enemy sign (specifically Gemini or Virgo = Mercury's signs, which are enemy to Mars)

claim.text: Mars in 10th in an enemy sign → early death of father. Specifically: Mars in 10th in Gemini (Sagittarius ASC) or Virgo (Capricorn ASC or Sagittarius ASC) = enemy sign for Mars (Mercury's signs). 'Early and doubtless' = high-strength indicator.

full_text: The Moon in the 6th, Saturn in the ascendant and Mars in the 7th — this array of heavenly bodies at birth will not ensure a long span of life for the father.

claim.text: Moon in 6th + Saturn in ASC + Mars in 7th → father does not live long. (This is the inverse of rule 033 where same planets in same houses harm the native; here it harms the father.)

full_text: If the Sun is aspected by Saturn and is in Aries/Scorpio Navamsa, the father would have given up the family before the birth of the child or would have passed away.

condition.subject: Sun
condition.additional: Sun aspected by Saturn + Sun in Aries or Scorpio Navamsa (D9)

claim.text: Sun aspected by Saturn + Sun in Aries or Scorpio Navamsa → father abandoned family before native's birth OR father died before/around birth. The D9 sign confirmation (Aries/Scorpio Navamsa) is required alongside the natal aspect.

full_text: If the 4th, 10th and 12th are all occupied by malefics, both the parents will leave the child to its own fate and wander from place to place.

condition.subject: malefic
condition.additional: Malefics in all three: 4th, 10th AND 12th simultaneously

claim.text: Malefics in 4th + 10th + 12th → both parents abandon the child (wander away). 4th (mother) + 9th/10th axis (father/career) + 12th (loss/foreign) all afflicted = parental abandonment or wandering.

full_text: The father will not see the native till his (the native's) 23rd year if Rahu and Jupiter are together in an inimical sign identical with the ascendant or the 4th. Inimical signs for Jupiter = Mercury's or Venus's signs (Gemini, Virgo for Mercury; Taurus, Libra for Venus). Rahu is inimically placed in Cancer, Leo, Aries and Scorpio. Jupiter is friendly in these signs.

condition.subject: Rahu_Jupiter
condition.additional: Rahu+Jupiter together in an inimical sign for Jupiter (Gemini/Virgo/Taurus/Libra) in ASC or 4th

claim.text: Rahu + Jupiter conjunct in inimical sign (for Jupiter) placed in ASC or 4th → father absent from native's life till native's 23rd year. Inimical signs for Jupiter: Gemini, Virgo (Mercury's), Taurus, Libra (Venus's). Timing: separation/absence for first 23 years.

full_text: Ch09 tail (slokas 43-45 appearing in Ch10 PDF): The Sun is the indicator (significator/karaka) of father for ALL beings. The Moon is the indicator of mother. Should the Sun be aspected by malefics OR be hemmed between malefics, this will cause evils to the father. Similarly, the Moon is to be considered in respect of the mother. Malefics in the 6th, 8th or 4th from the Sun will bring inauspicious results about the father. Malefics in such places from the Moon will be adverse for the mother. The strength or otherwise of the occupants concerned be suitably estimated.

condition.subject: Sun_Moon_parental_karakas
condition.description: Sun = universal father karaka; Moon = universal mother karaka. Malefics in 4/6/8 from Sun = father affliction; same from Moon = mother affliction. Attributed to Ch09 slokas 43-45.

claim.text: Sun = father indicator for all natives. Moon = mother indicator. Malefics aspecting Sun OR Papakartari on Sun → evil to father. Malefics in 4th/6th/8th from Sun → inauspicious for father. Same rules apply to Moon for mother. Planetary strength at those positions must be assessed — a strong planet in 4/6/8 from Sun/Moon has more impact than a weak one.

full_text: Introduction: Those are the evils (due to a native). I now narrate the antidotes for such evils as well, which will be helpful to assess the extent of inauspiciousness. Note: The antidotes mentioned here are in the context of short life (Balarishta). While some antidotes may carry with them the concept of fortunate yogas, every principle does not.

condition.subject: antidote_scope
condition.description: Ch10 antidotes apply specifically in the context of short-life (Balarishta) evils from Ch09

claim.text: The antidotes in Ch10 are specifically for assessing extent of inauspiciousness from Balarishta (short-life evils). They reduce or nullify evils from Ch09. Not all antidotes indicate fortunate yogas — they primarily function as evil-mitigators. Engine should check antidotes AFTER identifying any Balarishta combination.

full_text: Should ONE among Mercury, Jupiter and Venus be in an angle (Kendra: 1st/4th/7th/10th) from the ascendant, all evils (Balarishta) are destroyed — as the Sun eliminates darkness.

condition.subject: benefic_in_kendra
condition.additional: Any ONE of Mercury/Jupiter/Venus in any Kendra (1/4/7/10)

claim.text: One benefic (Mercury OR Jupiter OR Venus) in any angular house (1/4/7/10) → ALL Balarishta evils destroyed. Single benefic in Kendra is sufficient to nullify all short-life yogas. This is the strongest and broadest antidote in Ch10.

full_text: A single but STRONG Jupiter in the ascendant will ward off all evils — as a single reverential obeisance before Lord Siva frees one from all sins. Exception: In the case of Capricorn ascendant, Jupiter therein should be exceedingly strong by other virtues (e.g. exaltation, own sign, etc.), as a weak Jupiter in Capricorn (its debilitation sign) can lead to short life. Sage Bhrigu hints at medium span of life (Madhyayu) when Jupiter is in the ascendant identical with debilitation OR inimical sign OR a malefic's sign.

condition.subject: Jupiter
condition.additional: Jupiter strong in ASC. Exception: Capricorn ASC — Jupiter in debilitation/inimical/malefic sign gives medium life, not full protection.

claim.text: Strong Jupiter in ASC → all Balarishta evils warded off. Condition: Jupiter must be STRONG (not debilitated, inimical, or in malefic sign). Exception for Capricorn ASC: Jupiter in Capricorn (debilitation) needs extra strength from other sources; otherwise gives Madhyayu (medium span), not full antidote.

full_text: The ascendant lord is singly capable of counteracting all evils if he is strongly placed in an angle — as Lord Siva destroyed the three cities.

condition.subject: ascendant_lord
condition.additional: Lagna lord (ASC lord) strongly placed in any Kendra (1/4/7/10)

claim.text: ASC lord strongly in any angular house (Kendra 1/4/7/10) → all Balarishta evils counteracted. The lagna lord's strength and Kendra placement is a self-sufficient antidote. 'Strongly placed' = not debilitated, not combust, not in enemy sign, with adequate Shadbala.

full_text: All evils are destroyed if a BENEFIC aspects the ascendant of one born during NIGHT in the BRIGHT HALF (Shukla Paksha = waxing Moon fortnight). Similarly, a MALEFIC's aspect on the ascendant of one born during DAY TIME in the DARK HALF (Krishna Paksha = waning Moon fortnight) also destroys all evils.

condition.subject: birth_conditions
condition.additional: Two conditions: (A) Night birth + Shukla Paksha + benefic aspects ASC; (B) Day birth + Krishna Paksha + malefic aspects ASC

claim.text: Antidote A: Night birth + Shukla Paksha (waxing fortnight) + benefic aspecting ASC → all Balarishta evils destroyed. Antidote B: Day birth + Krishna Paksha (waning fortnight) + malefic aspecting ASC → all Balarishta evils destroyed. Both conditions are time-of-birth + lunar phase sensitive.

full_text: Antidote rationale: Night and bright half are congruent (both are times of Moon's strength). Benefic aspect on ASC in such congruent conditions maximises the protective potential. Day and dark half are also congruent in a different polarity sense (solar day + dark fortnight = malefic affinity context). A malefic aspecting ASC in this second context paradoxically destroys evils — perhaps because the malefic acts in its natural domain and neutralises the evil rather than adding to it.

condition.subject: antidote_rationale
condition.description: Explanatory note on the night/bright-half benefic ASC antidote and day/dark-half malefic ASC antidote logic

claim.text: Night + Shukla Paksha = Moon-congruent conditions: benefic on ASC maximises protection. Day + Krishna Paksha = Sun-congruent/malefic-affinity context: malefic on ASC in its natural polarity destroys the evil. Both represent conditions where the aspecting planet operates in its strongest natural context.

full_text: Ch09 tail extended note from Ch10 PDF: Malefics in 6th/8th/4th from the Sun → inauspicious results about the father (generalised rule beyond the specific Balarishta context). The parent-significator rules (Sun=father, Moon=mother) are valid for the entire lifespan assessment, not just Balarishta. Attributed to Ch09 slokas 43-45.

condition.subject: malefic
condition.additional: Malefics in 4th/6th/8th from Sun → father; same from Moon → mother

claim.text: Malefics in 4th, 6th, or 8th counted from the Sun → inauspicious for father throughout life. Malefics in 4th, 6th, or 8th from the Moon → adverse for mother. Strength of those planets must be estimated. Rule applies universally (not just Balarishta). Cross-reference: Ch09 rules 033-041 for specific father-affliction yogas.

full_text: Antidote precedence and hierarchy: The antidotes in Ch10 operate as follows — (1) Any ONE benefic (Mercury/Jupiter/Venus) in any Kendra = full neutralisation; (2) Strong Jupiter in ASC alone = full neutralisation; (3) ASC lord strongly in Kendra = full neutralisation; (4) Night birth Shukla Paksha + benefic on ASC = full neutralisation; (5) Day birth Krishna Paksha + malefic on ASC = full neutralisation. Any one of these conditions appearing in a chart with Balarishta yogas will destroy those evils.

condition.subject: antidote_hierarchy
condition.description: Engine logic: check all 5 antidote conditions after detecting any Balarishta yoga. Any single match = Balarishta destroyed.

claim.text: Engine check order for Balarishta antidotes: (1) Mercury/Jupiter/Venus in Kendra? (2) Strong Jupiter in 1st? (3) Lagna lord strong in Kendra? (4) Night+Shukla Paksha+benefic on ASC? (5) Day+Krishna Paksha+malefic on ASC? If any = YES → Balarishta nullified. If ALL = NO → Balarishta operative.

title: 1st House Primary Significations
summary: The 1st house governs the native's physical body, appearance, intellect, vitality, and innate temperament.
full_text: The 1st house (Ascendant/Lagna) is the primary reference for physique, bodily appearance, intellect (and the organ of intelligence, i.e. the brain), complexion of the body, vigour, weakness, happiness, grief, and the innate nature of the native.

result.effect: The 1st house indicates: physique, appearance, intellect, complexion, vigour, weakness, happiness, grief, and innate nature.

title: 2nd House Primary Significations
summary: The 2nd house governs wealth, family, food, and material resources.
full_text: The 2nd house signifies wealth, grains and food, family, death, enemies, metals, and precious stones.

result.effect: The 2nd house indicates: wealth, grains/food, family, death, enemies, metals, and precious stones.

title: 3rd House Primary Significations
summary: The 3rd house governs courage, siblings, servants, short journeys, and initiatory rites.
full_text: The 3rd house signifies valour/courage, servants and attendants, brothers and sisters (coborn), initiatory instructions (diksha/upadesha), journeys, and the death of parents.

result.effect: The 3rd house indicates: valour, servants, brothers and sisters, initiatory instructions, journeys, and death of parents.

title: 4th House Primary Significations
summary: The 4th house governs mother, home, property, conveyances, and domestic happiness.
full_text: The 4th house signifies conveyances, relatives, mother, happiness, treasure, lands, and houses/property.

result.effect: The 4th house indicates: conveyances, relatives, mother, happiness, treasure, lands, and houses.

title: 5th House Primary Significations
summary: The 5th house governs progeny, intellect, spiritual merit, and royal authority.
full_text: The 5th house signifies amulets (kavachas), sacred spells (mantras), learning, knowledge, sons/progeny, royalty and authority, and fall of position. It is the house of purva punya (accumulated merit from past lives).

result.effect: The 5th house indicates: amulets, sacred spells, learning, knowledge, progeny, royalty/authority, and fall of position.

title: 6th House Primary Significations
summary: The 6th house governs enemies, disease, debts, and service.
full_text: The 6th house signifies maternal uncle, doubts about death, enemies, ulcers/bodily injuries, and step-mother. It is a dusthana (malefic house) associated with disease, debt, and adversaries.

result.effect: The 6th house indicates: maternal uncle, doubts about death, enemies, ulcers/injuries, and step-mother.

title: 7th House Primary Significations
summary: The 7th house governs spouse, partnerships, travel, and trade.
full_text: The 7th house signifies wife/spouse, travel, trade and business, loss of sight, and death. It is the house of Kalatra (spouse) and all one-to-one partnerships.

result.effect: The 7th house indicates: wife/spouse, travel, trade/business, loss of sight, and death.

title: 8th House Primary Significations
summary: The 8th house governs longevity, hidden matters, death, and events across lifetimes.
full_text: The 8th house signifies longevity, battle, enemies, forts/fortifications, wealth of the deceased, and things that have happened and are yet to happen — encompassing both past and future births. It is the primary house for assessing lifespan.

result.effect: The 8th house indicates: longevity, battle, enemies, forts, wealth of the deceased, and events across past and future births.

title: 9th House Primary Significations
summary: The 9th house governs fortune, dharma, religion, and the father's relatives.
full_text: The 9th house signifies fortunes and affluence, wife's brother, religion and dharma, brother's wife, and visits to sacred shrines. It is the Bhagya (fortune) and Dharma (righteous conduct) bhava.

result.effect: The 9th house indicates: fortunes, wife's brother, religion/dharma, brother's wife, and visits to sacred shrines.

title: 10th House Primary Significations
summary: The 10th house governs profession, career, authority, father, and public standing.
full_text: The 10th house signifies royalty and authority, place/status, profession and livelihood, honour, father (in the context of the native's duty and last rites towards father), living in foreign lands, and debts. Note: the father as an individual is primarily studied from the 9th house; the 10th shows the native's professional relationship with father's legacy and status.

result.effect: The 10th house indicates: royalty/authority, place, profession/livelihood, honour, father (status/duties), living abroad, and debts.

title: 11th House Primary Significations
summary: The 11th house governs gains, income, fulfilment of desires, and elder siblings.
full_text: The 11th house signifies all articles and gains, son's wife (daughter-in-law), income, prosperity, and quadrupeds. It is the Labha (gains) bhava and is the primary house for assessing one's financial inflows and fulfilment of desires.

result.effect: The 11th house indicates: all gains/articles, son's wife, income, prosperity, and quadrupeds.

title: 12th House Primary Significations
summary: The 12th house governs expenses, losses, liberation, and the fate after death.
full_text: The 12th house signifies expenses, the history of enemies, and one's own death and final liberation (moksha). It is the Vyaya (loss/expenditure) bhava and relates to confinement, foreign residence, and spiritual liberation.

result.effect: The 12th house indicates: expenses, history of enemies, one's own death, and final liberation (moksha).

title: Bhava Prospers — Benefic Occupies or Aspects the House
summary: A house flourishes when a natural benefic planet occupies or aspects it.
full_text: Predict prosperity of a house/bhava which is conjunct or aspected by a natural benefic planet (Jupiter, Venus, well-placed Mercury, or waxing Moon). The presence or aspect of a benefic is the most direct indicator of the bhava's wellbeing.

result.effect: A bhava occupied by or aspected by a natural benefic planet flourishes and gives positive results for that bhava's significations.

title: Bhava Prospers — Lord in Yuvavastha or Kaumaravastha
summary: A house prospers when its lord occupies the degrees of Yuvavastha or Kaumaravastha.
full_text: A bhava flourishes when its lord is in Yuvavastha (12°–18° of an odd sign; or 12°–18° of an even sign) or Kaumaravastha (6°–12° of an odd sign; or 18°–24° of an even sign). These states indicate the planet is in an active, vigorous phase and can fully express its significations for the bhava.

result.effect: A bhava whose lord is in Yuvavastha or Kaumaravastha will flourish and produce strong positive results for its significations.

title: Bhava Prospers — Lord in Prabuddhavastha (Own Sign or Exaltation)
summary: A house prospers when its lord is in its own sign or exaltation sign (Prabuddhavastha).
full_text: A bhava flourishes when its lord is in Prabuddhavastha, also called Jagradavastha (wakeful state) — meaning the lord is placed in its own sign or in its exaltation sign. A planet in debilitation or combustion is explicitly excluded: the good results are void in those states. For planets owning two houses, the Moolatrikona house benefits most directly.

result.effect: A bhava whose lord is in own sign or exaltation (Prabuddhavastha) flourishes strongly. This benefit is void if the lord is debilitated or combust.

title: Bhava Prospers — Lord Placed in the 10th House
summary: A house gains strength when its lord is in the 10th house from the ascendant.
full_text: A bhava gains strength and produces good results when its lord is placed in the 10th house from the ascendant. The 10th house is the strongest Kendra (angular house) and elevates the lord's capacity to benefit its owned bhava.

result.effect: A bhava whose lord is placed in the 10th house from the ascendant gains strength and produces auspicious results for that bhava's significations.

title: Bhava Annihilated — Lord Joins Malefic and Bhava Unaspected by Its Lord
summary: A house suffers when it receives no aspect from its own lord AND the lord is associated with a malefic.
full_text: A bhava suffers annihilation when two conditions coincide: (1) the bhava is not aspected by its own lord, and (2) the bhava lord associates (by conjunction or aspect) with a malefic planet. The absence of the lord's protective aspect combined with malefic association significantly harms the bhava's significations.

result.effect: A bhava is harmed when it receives no aspect from its own lord and the lord is simultaneously associated with a malefic planet.

title: Bhava Annihilated — Lord Associates with Dusthana Lords
summary: A house suffers when its lord associates with the lords of the 3rd, 6th, 8th, 11th, or 12th houses.
full_text: A bhava is harmed when its lord associates with one of the lords of the malefic houses — specifically the lords of the 3rd, 6th, 8th, 11th (upachaya with a mischievous quality), and 12th houses. Such association transfers the adverse quality of those house lords to the bhava under consideration.

result.effect: A bhava suffers when its lord associates with lords of the 3rd, 6th, 8th, 11th, or 12th houses.

title: Bhava Annihilated — Lord Defeated in Grahayuddha (Planetary War)
summary: A house suffers when its lord is defeated in a planetary war (Grahayuddha).
full_text: A bhava is harmed when its lord is defeated in Grahayuddha (planetary war) — a state occurring when two non-luminary planets are within approximately 1° of each other and the planet with lesser brightness or southern latitude is considered defeated. A defeated planet cannot effectively protect or support its owned bhava.

result.effect: A bhava is harmed when its lord is defeated in Grahayuddha (planetary war). The defeated lord cannot sustain its bhava's significations.

title: Bhava Weakened — Lord in Vriddhavastha (Aged State)
summary: A house gives ineffective results when its lord is in Vriddhavastha (the aged or declining state).
full_text: A bhava gives diminished results when its lord is in Vriddhavastha (old or aged state): occupying 18°–24° of an odd sign or 6°–12° of an even sign. A planet in this state is declining in effectiveness and cannot fully support the bhava it owns.

result.effect: A bhava whose lord is in Vriddhavastha (18°–24° of an odd sign; or 6°–12° of an even sign) gives weakened and ineffective results.

title: Bhava Destroyed — Lord in Mritavastha (Dead State)
summary: A house is effectively destroyed when its lord is in Mritavastha (the dead or expired state).
full_text: A bhava is destroyed when its lord is in Mritavastha (dead state): occupying the last 6° of an odd sign (24°–30°) or the first 6° of an even sign (0°–6°). A planet in this state is inert and cannot produce beneficial results for its owned bhava.

result.effect: A bhava whose lord is in Mritavastha (last 6° of odd sign; or first 6° of even sign) is destroyed and produces no beneficial results.

title: Bhava Neutralised — Lord in Suptavastha (Sleeping/Dormant State)
summary: A house's effects are suppressed when its lord is in Suptavastha — debilitated or placed in an inimical sign.
full_text: A bhava's results are neutralised or suppressed when its lord is in Suptavastha (sleeping state), which applies to a planet that is debilitated or placed in an inimical sign. In this state the planet cannot actively support its owned bhava and the bhava's significations remain dormant or unexpressed.

result.effect: A bhava whose lord is in Suptavastha (debilitated or in inimical sign) has its effects neutralised or suppressed; the bhava's significations remain dormant.

sloka_ref: BPHS Vol 1, Ch25, slokas 1 + Santhanam notes
source_text: Non-luminous planets (Upagrahas) covered in this chapter: Dhuma, Vyatipata, Paridhi (Pariyesha), Chapa (Indra Dhanus/Kodanda), Dhwaja (Sikhi/Upaketu), Gulika, Pranapada. Comparison assignments from Santhanam notes: Gulika is compared to Saturn; Kala to Rahu; Ardha Prahara to Mercury; Yamaghantaka to Jupiter.
result: Engine must compute and store positions for the following non-luminous planets/sensitive points: Dhuma, Vyatipata, Paridhi (Pariyesha), Chapa (Indra Dhanus/Kodanda), Dhwaja (Sikhi/Upaketu), Gulika, Pranapada. For interpretation, these planets are analogised to: Gulika=Saturn-like, Kala=Rahu-like, Ardha Prahara=Mercury-like, Yamaghantaka=Jupiter-like.
notes: TT-CH25-01: Confirm engine has Upagraha position computation for all seven planets listed. Computation formulas are given elsewhere in BPHS (cross-reference Ch3 slokas 66-69 per Santhanam notes). Kala and Ardha Prahara also exist as Upagrahas but their house effects are not in Ch25 — they appear in the comparison context only.

sloka_ref: BPHS Vol 1, Ch25, Santhanam notes on sloka 2
source_text: The first two (Dhuma and Kala) are malefic in nature while the latter two (Ardha Prahara and Yamaghantaka) are benefics. Of all, Gulika is the most powerful in adverse results while Yamaghantaka (son of Jupiter) is the mighty benefic.
result: Malefic Upagrahas: Dhuma, Kala (and by extension Gulika as most powerful malefic). Benefic Upagrahas: Ardha Prahara, Yamaghantaka (most powerful benefic). Gulika > all other Upagrahas in magnitude of adverse results. Yamaghantaka > all others in benefic results. This polarity classification modifies the engine's weighting of Upagraha effects.
notes: Gulika is the most critical Upagraha for adverse interpretation — engine must weight Gulika effects higher than other Upagrahas in adverse contexts. Santhanam calls Gulika 'son of Saturn', reinforcing its Saturn-like malefic nature.

sloka_ref: BPHS Vol 1, Ch25, Santhanam notes on sloka 2
source_text: The results due to Dhuma, Gulika etc. will mature in the Dasa periods of their dispositors. For example, if Gulika is placed in Virgo, the effects due to Gulika will come to pass in the major and sub-periods of Mercury.
result: Timing rule: Effects of all Upagrahas (Dhuma, Gulika, etc.) manifest primarily in the Vimshottari Dasha and Antardasha of the planet that rules the sign occupied by the Upagraha (the dispositor). The engine must compute the dispositor of each Upagraha and tag its effects with the dispositor's Dasha period.
notes: This is a universal timing rule for all Upagrahas. Engine implementation: for each Upagraha house effect, tag timing_planet = sign_lord(upagraha_sign). Effects fire in that planet's Dasha/Antardasha windows.

sloka_ref: BPHS Vol 1, Ch25, Santhanam notes on sloka 2
source_text: For lordships (or secondary lordships) of these also, consider each sign. For example, Gulika is 'lord' of Aquarius. Hence in the case of a Cancer native, he is the '8th lord' apart from Saturn's candidacy for 8th lordship. Of course primary importance be given to Saturn and he should not be underrated in that case.
result: Upagrahas have sign lordships that can be used for house lordship analysis. Gulika is lord of Aquarius. When an Upagraha lords a bhava, it acts as a secondary lord of that house — interpret its placement as that lord's placement. Primary importance remains with the traditional planetary lord (e.g., Saturn as primary 8th lord for Cancer lagna, Gulika as secondary).
notes: TT-CH25-02: Confirm complete sign lordship table for all Upagrahas (Dhuma, Vyatipata, Paridhi, Chapa, Dhwaja, Gulika, Pranapada). Santhanam references Ch3 slokas 66-69 and Keeranuru Nataraja's Jetakaslankaram for this data. Currently only Gulika = Aquarius lord is confirmed from this extract.

source_text: O Brahmin, these are the effects for Dhooma etc. Before declaring results, consider the Sun's relation and other planets' positions and aspects apart from their strength or weakness.
result: Before applying Upagraha house effects, the engine must evaluate the dispositor of each Upagraha. If the dispositor is well-placed, well-aspected, or strong: adverse Upagraha effects are reduced; benefic effects are amplified. If the dispositor is weak or adversely placed: benefic effects are reduced; adverse effects are amplified. Additionally, Upagraha effects must be balanced against the effects of Sun through Saturn (and nodes) in the same house/context.
notes: This is the master moderation rule for all Ch25 Upagraha effects. Engine must: (1) compute dispositor strength for each Upagraha; (2) apply the dispositor modifier to scale the effect magnitude up or down; (3) cross-reference with planetary effects from Sun-Saturn+nodes in the same bhava for net assessment.

sloka_ref: BPHS Vol 1, Ch25, Santhanam notes on sloka 62
source_text: Out of all the non-luminous planets, Gulika deserves a special consideration in natal horoscopy as well as horary astrology. This is also a very important factor in birth rectification and such other important calculations.
result: Gulika has elevated priority among all Upagrahas. The engine must assign higher interpretive weight to Gulika in natal chart analysis and flag Gulika's position as a high-priority data point for horary queries and birth time rectification calculations.
notes: Santhanam explicitly singles out Gulika for special consideration — Gulika's house effects (rules 067-078) should be weighted most heavily among all Upagrahas in the engine's output.

source_text: If Dhuma is in the ascendant, the native will be valiant, endowed with beautiful eyes, stupefied in disposition, unkind, wicked and highly short-tempered.
result: The native is valiant and endowed with beautiful eyes, but is stupefied in disposition, unkind, wicked, and highly short-tempered.
notes: Mixed: physical beauty and valour alongside moral negatives. Timing: dispositor's Dasha per rule 003.

source_text: If Dhuma is in the 2nd, the native will be sickly, wealthy, devoid of a limb, will incur humiliation at royal level, be dull-witted and be a eunuch.
result: The native is sickly, devoid of a limb, incurs humiliation at the royal level, is dull-witted, and is a eunuch. Despite these afflictions, the native is wealthy.
notes: Wealth coexists with significant bodily and social afflictions. 'Eunuch' (kliba) — may indicate sexual incapacity or gender role irregularity in classical context.

source_text: If Dhuma is in the 3rd, the native will be intelligent, very bold, delighted, eloquent, and be endowed with men and wealth.
result: The native is intelligent, very bold, delighted, eloquent, and endowed with followers and wealth.
notes: Fully positive — unusual for a malefic Upagraha. 3rd house is natural house of courage/communication, aligned with these effects.

source_text: If Dhuma is in the 4th, the native will be grieved on account of being given up by his female, but will be learned in all sastras.
result: The native is grieved due to being abandoned or rejected by a female (wife or mother), but is learned in all scriptures (sastras).
notes: Mixed: learning offset by domestic/marital grief. 'Female who gives up' could mean wife, mother, or both — 4th house governs both.

source_text: If Dhuma is in the 5th, the native will have limited progeny, be devoid of wealth, be great, will eat anything and be bereft of friends and Mantras.
result: The native has limited progeny, is devoid of wealth, bereft of friends and Mantras (sacred knowledge), and eats indiscriminately. The native is nonetheless great (honoured or eminent).
notes: 'Bereft of Mantras' implies lack of sacred learning or ritual knowledge. 'Will eat anything' = no dietary discrimination, a classical negative character trait.

source_text: If Dhuma is in the 6th, the native will be strong, will conquer his enemies, be very brilliant, famous and free from diseases.
result: The native is strong, conquers enemies, is very brilliant, famous, and free from diseases.
notes: Fully positive. Malefic Upagraha in 6th (dusthana) produces positive results — consistent with classical principle that malefics thrive in the 3rd/6th/11th.

source_text: If Dhuma is in the 7th, the native will be penniless, ever sensuous, skilful in going to others' females and be always devoid of brilliance.
result: The native is penniless, ever sensuous, inclined towards others' women, and always devoid of brilliance.
notes: Uniformly negative. 7th house placement harms marital fidelity and financial standing.

source_text: If Dhuma is in the 8th, the native will be bereft of courage but enthusiastic, truthful, disagreeable, hard-hearted and selfish.
result: The native lacks courage but is enthusiastic, truthful, disagreeable, hard-hearted, and selfish.
notes: Mixed: truthfulness and enthusiasm offset by cowardice, disagreeableness, selfishness.

source_text: If Dhuma is in the 9th, the native will be endowed with sons and fortunes, be rich, honourable, kind, religious, and well-disposed to his relatives.
result: The native is endowed with sons and good fortune, is rich, honourable, kind, religious, and well-disposed to relatives.
notes: Fully positive. Malefic Upagraha in the 9th (dharma house) gives positive results — likely mitigated by the trine's auspicious nature.

source_text: If Dhuma is in the 10th, the native will be endowed with sons and fortunes, be delighted, intelligent, happy and truthful.
result: The native is endowed with sons and fortune, is delighted, intelligent, happy, and truthful.
notes: Fully positive. Dhuma in 10th and 9th both yield similar positive results — sons, fortunes, good character.

source_text: If Dhuma is in the 11th, the native will be endowed with wealth, grains and gold, be beautiful, will have knowledge of arts, be modest and be skilful in singing.
result: The native is endowed with wealth, grains, and gold, is beautiful, knowledgeable in arts, modest, and skilful in singing.
notes: Fully positive. 11th house (gains) consistently gives positive results for this Upagraha.

source_text: If Dhuma is in the 12th, the native will be morally fallen, will indulge in sinful acts, be interested in others' wives, addicted to vices, unkind and crafty.
result: The native is morally fallen, indulges in sinful acts, is interested in others' women, addicted to vices, unkind, and crafty.
notes: Uniformly negative. 12th house = moral and spiritual decline with Dhuma.

source_text: If Vyatipata is in the ascendant, the native will be troubled by miseries, be cruel, will indulge in destructive acts, be foolish and will be ill-disposed to his relatives.
result: The native is troubled by miseries, cruel, indulges in destructive acts, is foolish, and is ill-disposed towards relatives.
notes: Uniformly negative in the ascendant.

source_text: If Vyatipata is in the 2nd, the native will be morally crooked, bilious, will enjoy pleasures, be eloquent, be wicked and sinful.
result: The native is morally crooked, bilious (pitta disorder), enjoys pleasures, is eloquent, wicked, and sinful.
notes: Mixed: enjoyment of pleasures and eloquence amid moral and health negatives.

source_text: If Vyatipata is in the 3rd, the native will be firm in disposition, be a warrior, be liberal, very rich, dear to king, and be head of an army.
result: The native is firm in disposition, a warrior, liberal, very rich, dear to the king, and head of an army.
notes: Fully positive. Consistent with malefic Upagrahas performing well in the 3rd house.

source_text: If Vyatipata is in the 4th, the native will be endowed with relatives etc. but not sons and fortunes.
result: The native has relatives and associates but lacks sons and good fortune.
notes: Social connections preserved but progeny and fortune denied.

source_text: If Vyatipata is in the 5th, the native will be poor, charming in appearance, will have imbalances of phlegm, bile and wind, be hard-hearted and shameless.
result: The native is poor but charming in appearance, suffers from imbalances of phlegm, bile, and wind (tridosha disorders), is hard-hearted, and shameless.
notes: Mixed: physical charm offset by poverty, tridosha disorders, and character negatives. 'Phlegm/bile/wind' = kapha/pitta/vata in Ayurvedic classification.

source_text: If Vyatipata is in the 6th, the native will destroy his enemies, be physically mighty, skilful in use of all kinds of weapons and in arts, and be peaceful in disposition.
result: The native destroys enemies, is physically mighty, skilful in use of all weapons and arts, and peaceful in disposition.
notes: Fully positive. 6th house = enemy destruction and physical prowess for malefic Upagrahas.

source_text: If Vyatipata is in the 7th, the native will be bereft of wealth, wife and sons, will subdue to females, be miserable, sensuous, shameless and friendly to others.
result: The native is bereft of wealth, wife, and sons, submits to females, is miserable, sensuous, shameless, and overly friendly to others.
notes: Uniformly negative. 7th house with Vyatipata = comprehensive marital and financial adversity.

source_text: If Vyatipata is in the 8th, the native will have deformity of eyes, be ugly, unfortunate, spiteful to Brahmins and be troubled by disorders of blood.
result: The native has deformity of eyes, is ugly, unfortunate, spiteful to Brahmins, and troubled by blood disorders.
notes: Uniformly negative. Eye deformity + blood disorders are specific physical markers.

source_text: If Vyatipata is in the 9th, the native will have many kinds of business and many friends, be very learned, well-disposed to his wife and be eloquent.
result: The native has many kinds of business and many friends, is very learned, well-disposed to wife, and eloquent.
notes: Fully positive. Trine house (9th) mitigates malefic Upagraha.

source_text: If Vyatipata is in the 10th, the native will be rich, religious, peaceful, skilful in religious acts, very learned and farsighted.
result: The native is rich, religious, peaceful, skilful in religious acts, very learned, and farsighted.
notes: Fully positive. 10th house placement of Vyatipata yields religion and learning-oriented positive effects.

source_text: If Vyatipata is in the 11th, the native will be extremely opulent, be honourable, truthful, firm in policy, endowed with many horses and be interested in singing.
result: The native is extremely opulent, honourable, truthful, firm in policy, endowed with many horses, and interested in singing.
notes: Fully positive. 'Many horses' = conveyances and wealth indicator in classical context.

source_text: If Vyatipata is in the 12th, the native will be given to anger, associated with many activities, disabled, irreligious and will hate his own relatives.
result: The native is given to anger, constantly engaged in many activities, disabled, irreligious, and hates own relatives.
notes: Uniformly negative. 'Disabled' implies physical impairment.

source_text: If Paridhi is in the ascendant, the native will be learned, truthful, peaceful, rich, endowed with sons, pure, charitable and dear to elders.
result: The native is learned, truthful, peaceful, rich, endowed with sons, pure, charitable, and dear to elders.
notes: Fully positive. Paridhi in the ascendant is notably auspicious — rare for an Upagraha.

source_text: If Paridhi is in the 2nd, the native will be wealthy, charming, will enjoy pleasures, be happy, very religious and be a lord.
result: The native is wealthy, charming, enjoys pleasures, is happy, very religious, and attains lordship.
notes: Fully positive.

source_text: If Paridhi is in the 3rd, the native will be fond of his wife, be very charming, pious, well-disposed to his men, be a servant and be respectful of his elders.
result: The native is fond of wife, very charming, pious, well-disposed to associates, respectful of elders; is in the position of a servant.
notes: Mostly positive but 'servant' is a status negative. In classical context 'servant' (dasa) may mean subservient position, employed status, or devotional service — not necessarily pejorative.

source_text: If Paridhi is in the 4th, the native will be wonderstruck, helpful to enemies as well, kind, endowed with everything and be skilful in singing.
result: The native is of a wonderstruck (marvelling) nature, helpful even to enemies, kind, endowed with all comforts, and skilful in singing.
notes: Fully positive. 'Helpful to enemies' is a mark of universal compassion, not a negative.

source_text: If Paridhi is in the 5th, the native will be affluent, virtuous, splendorous, affectionate, religious and dear to his wife.
result: The native is affluent, virtuous, splendorous, affectionate, religious, and dear to wife.
notes: Fully positive.

source_text: If Paridhi is in the 6th, the native will be famous and wealthy, be endowed with sons and pleasures, be helpful to all and will conquer his enemies.
result: The native is famous and wealthy, endowed with sons and pleasures, helpful to all, and conquers enemies.
notes: Fully positive.

source_text: If Paridhi is in the 7th, the native will have a limited number of children, be devoid of happiness, be of mediocre intelligence, very hard-hearted, and will have a sickly wife.
result: The native has limited children, is devoid of happiness, mediocre in intelligence, very hard-hearted, and has a sickly wife.
notes: Uniformly negative. 7th house = harm to spouse and progeny.

source_text: If Paridhi is in the 8th, the native will be spiritually disposed, peaceful, strong-bodied, firm in decision, religious and entire.
result: The native is spiritually disposed, peaceful, strong-bodied, firm in decision, religious, and whole/complete (lacking nothing).
notes: 'Entire' (samagra) = complete, lacking nothing — a positive completeness indicator. 8th house with Paridhi gives spiritual and physical strength.

source_text: If Paridhi is in the 9th, the native will be endowed with sons, be happy, brilliant, very affluent, be devoid of excessive passion, be honourable and be happy with even an iota.
result: The native is endowed with sons, happy, brilliant, very affluent, devoid of excessive passion, honourable, and content with very little.
notes: 'Happy with even an iota' = contentment; devoid of excessive passion = mental equanimity. Strongly positive.

source_text: If Paridhi is in the 10th, the native will be versed in arts, will enjoy pleasures, be strong-bodied, and be learned in all sastras.
result: The native is versed in arts, enjoys pleasures, is strong-bodied, and learned in all scriptures.
notes: Fully positive.

source_text: If Paridhi is in the 11th, the native will enjoy pleasures through women, be virtuous, intelligent, dear to his people and will suffer disorders of digestive fire.
result: The native enjoys pleasures through women, is virtuous, intelligent, and dear to associates; suffers from disorders of digestive fire (weak agni/digestion).
notes: Mixed: positive social and pleasure outcomes alongside digestive health issue. 'Disorders of digestive fire' = weak agni in Ayurvedic terms, causing chronic digestive ailments.

source_text: If Paridhi is in the 12th, the native will always be a spendthrift, be miserable, firm and will dishonour elders.
result: The native is always a spendthrift, miserable, firm in resolve, and dishonours elders.
notes: Negative dominant. 'Firm' could be positive determination but is contextually negative here (obstinacy supporting disrespect and overspending).

source_text: If Chapa is in the ascendant, the native will be endowed with wealth, grains and gold, be grateful, agreeable and devoid of all afflictions.
result: The native is endowed with wealth, grains, and gold, is grateful, agreeable, and devoid of all afflictions.
notes: Fully positive. Chapa (Indra Dhanus/Kodanda) in the ascendant gives comprehensive positive results.

source_text: If Chapa is in the 2nd, the native will speak affably, be very rich, modest, learned, charming and religious.
result: The native speaks affably, is very rich, modest, learned, charming, and religious.
notes: Fully positive.

source_text: If Chapa is in the 3rd, the native will be a miser, be versed in many arts, will indulge in thieving, be devoid of some limb and be unfriendly.
result: The native is a miser, versed in many arts, inclined to theft, devoid of a limb, and unfriendly.
notes: Mixed: arts knowledge offset by negative character traits and physical impairment. 3rd house with Chapa is negative unlike other Upagrahas.

source_text: If Chapa is in the 4th, the native will be happy, endowed with quadrupeds, wealth, grains etc., be honoured by the king and be devoid of sickness.
result: The native is happy, endowed with quadrupeds (animals/conveyances), wealth, grains, is honoured by the king, and free from sickness.
notes: Fully positive.

source_text: If Chapa is in the 5th, the native will be splendorous, far-sighted, pious, affable and will acquire prosperity in all his undertakings.
result: The native is splendorous, far-sighted, pious, affable, and acquires prosperity in all undertakings.
notes: Fully positive.

source_text: If Chapa is in the 6th, the native will destroy his enemies, be happy, affectionate, pure and will achieve plentifulness in all his undertakings.
result: The native destroys enemies, is happy, affectionate, pure, and achieves plentifulness in all undertakings.
notes: Fully positive.

source_text: If Chapa is in the 7th, the native will be wealthy, endowed with all virtues, learned in sastras, religious, and agreeable.
result: The native is wealthy, endowed with all virtues, learned in scriptures, religious, and agreeable.
notes: Fully positive — unusual for most Upagrahas in the 7th.

source_text: If Chapa is in the 8th, the native will be interested in others' jobs, be cruel, interested in others' wives and one defective limb.
result: The native is interested in others' work (meddlesome), cruel, inclined towards others' women, and has one defective limb.
notes: Uniformly negative.

source_text: If Chapa is in the 9th, the native will perform penance, will take to religious observations, be highly learned, and be famous among men.
result: The native performs penance, takes to religious observations, is highly learned, and is famous among men.
notes: Fully positive. 9th house (dharma) brings religious and learned outcomes with Chapa.

source_text: If Chapa is in the 10th, the native will be endowed with many sons, abundant wealth, cows, buffaloes etc. and will be famous among men.
result: The native is endowed with many sons, abundant wealth, cattle (cows, buffaloes), and is famous among men.
notes: Fully positive. Cattle are wealth/prosperity indicators in classical context.

source_text: If Chapa is in the 11th, the native will be gainful, free from diseases, very fiery in disposition, affectionate to his wife and will have knowledge of mantras and weapons.
result: The native is gainful, free from diseases, very fiery in disposition, affectionate to wife, and has knowledge of mantras and weapons (missiles).
notes: Fully positive.

source_text: If Chapa is in the 12th, the native will be wicked, very honourable, evil in disposition, shameless, will go to others' females and be ever poor.
result: The native is wicked, evil in disposition, shameless, inclined towards others' women, and ever poor. Despite these negatives, the native is very honourable.
notes: Mixed: 'very honourable' is an unusual positive in an otherwise negative result for 12th house Chapa. May indicate social reputation not matching inner character.

source_text: If Dhwaja is in the ascendant, the native will be skilful in all branches of learning, be happy, efficient in speech, agreeable and be very affectionate.
result: The native is skilful in all branches of learning, happy, efficient in speech, agreeable, and very affectionate.
notes: Fully positive. Dhwaja (Sikhi/Upaketu) in ascendant gives excellent learning and communication outcomes.
