source_text: If Dhwaja is in the 2nd, the native will be a good and affable speaker, be splendorous, will write poetry, be scholarly, honourable, modest and endowed with conveyances.
result: The native is a good and affable speaker, splendorous, writes poetry, is scholarly, honourable, modest, and endowed with conveyances.
notes: Fully positive. Strong 2nd house (speech, learning) effects.

source_text: If Dhwaja is in the 3rd, the native will be miserly, cruel in acts, thin-bodied, poor and will incur severe diseases.
result: The native is miserly, cruel in acts, thin-bodied, poor, and incurs severe diseases.
notes: Uniformly negative. 3rd house with Dhwaja is negative unlike most Upagrahas.

source_text: If Dhwaja is in the 4th, the native will be charming, very virtuous, gentle, interested in Vedas and be always happy.
result: The native is charming, very virtuous, gentle, interested in the Vedas, and always happy.
notes: Fully positive.

source_text: If Dhwaja is in the 5th, the native will be happy, will enjoy pleasures, be versed in arts, skilled in expedients, intelligent, eloquent and will respect elders.
result: The native is happy, enjoys pleasures, is versed in arts, skilled in expedients, intelligent, eloquent, and respects elders.
notes: Fully positive.

source_text: If Dhwaja is in the 6th, the native will be ominous for maternal relatives, will win over his enemies, be endowed with many relatives, valiant, splendorous and skilful.
result: The native is ominous for maternal relatives (brings harm or misfortune to them), wins over enemies, is endowed with many relatives, valiant, splendorous, and skilful.
notes: Mixed: maternal relative harm offset by enemy conquest and personal strength. 'Ominous for maternal relatives' is a specific harm indicator for the maternal family line.

source_text: If Dhwaja is in the 7th, the native will be interested in gambling, be sensuous, will enjoy pleasures and will befriend prostitutes.
result: The native is interested in gambling, sensuous, enjoys pleasures, and befriends prostitutes.
notes: Uniformly negative for marital/moral character.

source_text: If Dhwaja is in the 8th, the native will be interested in base acts, be sinful, shameless, will blame others, will lack in marital happiness and will take others' side.
result: The native is interested in base acts, sinful, shameless, blames others, lacks marital happiness, and takes others' side (disloyal to own).
notes: Uniformly negative.

source_text: If Dhwaja is in the 9th, the native will wear religious badges, be delighted, helpfully disposed to all and be skilled in religious deeds.
result: The native wears religious badges (marks of devotion), is delighted, helpfully disposed to all, and skilled in religious deeds.
notes: Fully positive. 9th house = religious/dharmic outcomes for Dhwaja.

source_text: O Brahmin, if Dhwaja is in the 10th, the native will be endowed with happiness and fortunes, be fond of females, be charitable and will befriend Brahmins.
result: The native is endowed with happiness and fortune, fond of females, charitable, and befriends Brahmins (learned people).
notes: Fully positive. 'Befriends Brahmins' = associates with learned/spiritual people.

source_text: If Dhwaja is in the 11th, the native will ever acquire gains, be very religious, honourable, affluent, fortunate, valiant and skilled in sacrificial rites.
result: The native ever acquires gains, is very religious, honourable, affluent, fortunate, valiant, and skilled in sacrificial rites.
notes: Fully positive. 11th house = continuous gain with Dhwaja.

source_text: If Dhwaja is in the 12th, the native will be interested in sinful acts, be valiant, untrustworthy, unkind, interested in others' females and be short-tempered.
result: The native is interested in sinful acts, valiant, untrustworthy, unkind, interested in others' women, and short-tempered.
notes: Mixed: valour is positive; all other outcomes are negative.

sloka_ref: BPHS Vol 1, Ch25, sloka 62 + Santhanam notes
source_text: If Gulika is in the ascendant, the native will be afflicted by diseases, be lustful, sinful, crafty, wicked and very miserable. Additionally (Santhanam notes): severe defects of eyes, will take to bad acts like thieving, disregards religion, deprived of progeny, dull-headed, longevity severely cut.
result: The native is afflicted by diseases, lustful, sinful, crafty, wicked, and very miserable. Additionally: severe eye defects, thieving tendencies, disregards religion, deprived of progeny, dull-headed, and severely shortened longevity.
notes: Strongly negative — Gulika in the ascendant is the most adverse Upagraha placement. Longevity cut is a severe indicator. Engine should treat Gulika in 1st as a high-weight adverse flag. Santhanam notes add significantly to the severity.

sloka_ref: BPHS Vol 1, Ch25, sloka 63 + Santhanam notes
source_text: If Gulika is in the 2nd, the native will be unsightly in appearance, miserable, mean, given to vices, shameless and penniless. Santhanam notes: unfortunate, learning obstructed, speech defects, harsh in speech, lives away from people, no family happiness, scandalous, unfit to counsel others, face troubles equal to death in 2nd lord's Dasha.
result: The native is unsightly, miserable, mean, given to vices, shameless, and penniless. Additionally: unfortunate, learning obstructed, speech defects, harsh speech, lives apart from family, no family happiness, scandalous, and faces troubles equal to death in the 2nd lord's Dasha period.
notes: Strongly negative. 2nd house (speech, learning, family, wealth) is comprehensively afflicted by Gulika. The Dasha timing note (2nd lord's Dasha = death-like troubles) is important for timing prediction.

sloka_ref: BPHS Vol 1, Ch25, sloka 64 + Santhanam notes
source_text: If Gulika is in the 3rd, the native will be charming in appearance, will head a village, be fond of virtuous men, and be honoured by the king. Santhanam notes: destruction of co-born; though fairly rich, will feel distressed.
result: The native is charming in appearance, heads a village, is fond of virtuous men, and honoured by the king. However: co-born (siblings) face destruction, and though fairly rich, the native feels distressed.
notes: Mixed: positive social status and appearance offset by harm to siblings and inner distress. 3rd house (siblings, courage) = destruction of co-born despite personal honour.

sloka_ref: BPHS Vol 1, Ch25, sloka 65 + Santhanam notes
source_text: If Gulika is in the 4th, the native will be sickly, devoid of happiness, sinful and afflicted due to wind and bilious excesses. Santhanam notes: inimical to others including relatives, devoid of conveyances, no good house to live in, miserable last days, painful death after long confinement.
result: The native is sickly, devoid of happiness, sinful, and afflicted by vata and pitta disorders. Additionally: inimical to relatives, devoid of conveyances, lacks a good home, faces miserable last days, and painful death after long confinement.
notes: Strongly negative across health, happiness, family, and end-of-life. 'Painful death after long confinement' is a severe longevity indicator.

sloka_ref: BPHS Vol 1, Ch25, sloka 66 + Santhanam notes
source_text: If Gulika is in the 5th, the native will not be praiseworthy, be poor, short-lived, spiteful, mean, be a eunuch, be subdued by his wife and be a heterodox. Santhanam notes: progenic ability significantly affected; not pious; at disposal of wife.
result: The native is not praiseworthy, poor, short-lived, spiteful, mean, a eunuch, subdued by wife, and heterodox. Additionally: progenic ability significantly affected (unless Jupiter and 5th lord are favourable), not pious, completely at wife's disposal.
notes: Strongly negative. Gulika in 5th = short life + progeny denial. Santhanam notes a conditional rescue: if Jupiter and 5th lord are favourable, progeny may still occur. Engine should flag Jupiter+5th lord strength as mitigation for this rule.

sloka_ref: BPHS Vol 1, Ch25, sloka 67 + Santhanam notes
source_text: If Gulika is in the 6th, the native will be devoid of enemies, be strong-bodied, splendorous, liked by his wife, enthusiastic, very friendly and helpful in disposition. Santhanam notes: interested in controlling evil spirits and livelihood from such; obtains children; courageous; freedom from diseases if 6th house is a benefic sign.
result: The native is devoid of enemies, strong-bodied, splendorous, liked by wife, enthusiastic, and very friendly and helpful. Additionally: inclined toward spirit control practices; obtains children; courageous. Freedom from disease is conditional on the 6th house being a benefic sign.
notes: Positive. 6th house (dusthana) is where Gulika's malefic energy is channelled productively. 'Controlling evil spirits' = Tantric/exorcism practices — Gulika's Saturn-like nature channelled into occult mastery. Conditional: disease-free only if 6th house sign is a benefic sign (Taurus, Gemini, Cancer, Virgo, Libra, Sagittarius, Pisces).

sloka_ref: BPHS Vol 1, Ch25, sloka 68 + Santhanam notes
source_text: If Gulika is in the 7th, the native will subdue to his spouse, be sinful, will go to others' females, be emaciated, devoid of friendship and will live on wife's (or a female's) wealth. Santhanam notes: thrives on female's wealth or spouse's contributions; conjugal life gives no happiness; possibly more than one marriage; not much knowledge; incurs misunderstandings in public dealings.
result: The native submits to spouse, is sinful, goes to others' women, is emaciated, devoid of friendship, and lives on wife's or a female's wealth. Additionally: conjugal life brings no happiness; possibly multiple marriages; limited knowledge; misunderstandings in public dealings.
notes: Uniformly negative for marriage and financial independence. Financial dependency on female is a consistent theme.

sloka_ref: BPHS Vol 1, Ch25, sloka 69 + Santhanam notes
source_text: If Gulika is in the 8th, the native will be troubled by hunger, be miserable, cruel, very much short-tempered, very unkind, poor and bereft of good qualities. Santhanam notes: difficult to get a square meal; ugly face; diseased eyes; yellowish teeth; quite short in stature.
result: The native is troubled by hunger, miserable, cruel, very short-tempered, very unkind, poor, and bereft of good qualities. Additionally: difficulty obtaining even a square meal; ugly face; diseased eyes; yellowish teeth; very short stature.
notes: Strongly negative with specific physical markers. Gulika in 8th = extreme poverty and comprehensive physical affliction.

sloka_ref: BPHS Vol 1, Ch25, sloka 70 + Santhanam notes
source_text: If Gulika is in the 9th, the native will undergo many ordeals, be emaciated, will perform evil acts, be very unkind, sluggish and be a tale-bearer. Santhanam notes: devoid of paternal bliss and good fortunes; father passes away in childhood; none of native's undertakings bear fruits.
result: The native undergoes many ordeals, is emaciated, performs evil acts, is very unkind, sluggish, and a tale-bearer. Additionally: devoid of paternal bliss; father passes away in the native's childhood; none of the native's undertakings bear fruits.
notes: Strongly negative. 9th house (father, fortune) with Gulika = early paternal bereavement and lifelong frustration of efforts.

sloka_ref: BPHS Vol 1, Ch25, sloka 71 + Santhanam notes
source_text: If Gulika is in the 10th, the native will be endowed with sons, be happy, will enjoy many things, be fond of worshipping gods and fire and will practise meditation and religion. Santhanam notes: favourable for Yoga and Meditation; at one stage native may turn into a heterodox and discard his religious code.
result: The native is endowed with sons, happy, enjoys many comforts, fond of worshipping gods and fire, and practises meditation and religion. Notable: at some stage may turn heterodox and abandon the religious code entirely.
notes: Mixed: genuine positive (sons, happiness, spirituality) but Santhanam notes eventual religious apostasy as a shadow outcome. 10th house with Gulika is one of the few positive placements for this malefic Upagraha.

sloka_ref: BPHS Vol 1, Ch25, sloka 72 + Santhanam notes
source_text: If Gulika is in the 11th, the native will enjoy women, be a leader of men, be helpful to his relatives, be short in stature and be an emperor. Santhanam notes: company of many females; devoid of good character; enjoys progeny happiness; wealthy; charming in appearance.
result: The native enjoys many women, is a leader of men, helpful to relatives, short in stature, and attains emperor-like status. Additionally: company of many females; deficient in good character; enjoys progeny happiness; wealthy; charming.
notes: Mixed: high status and wealth alongside poor character. 'Emperor' combined with 'devoid of good character' is a notable tension. 11th house with Gulika is auspicious for material gains.

sloka_ref: BPHS Vol 1, Ch25, sloka 73 + Santhanam notes
source_text: If Gulika is in the 12th, the native will indulge in base deeds, be sinful, defective-limbed, unfortunate, indolent, and will join mean people. Santhanam notes: innumerable misfortunes, loss of wealth on evil missions; however enjoys progeny happiness.
result: The native indulges in base deeds, is sinful, defective-limbed, unfortunate, indolent, and associates with mean people. Additionally: innumerable misfortunes and wealth loss through evil activities. Despite this, the native enjoys progeny happiness.
notes: Predominantly negative. The progeny happiness exception is notable — Santhanam explicitly notes it as a silver lining despite comprehensive adversity.

sloka_ref: BPHS Vol 1, Ch25, sloka 74 + Santhanam notes
source_text: If Pranapada is in the ascendant, the native will be weak, sickly, dumb, lunatic, dull-witted, defective-limbed, miserable and emaciated. Santhanam notes: Pranapada is a special ascendant calculated as a sensitive point — computation details on p.47.
result: The native is weak, sickly, dumb, lunatic, dull-witted, defective-limbed, miserable, and emaciated.
notes: TT-CH25-03: Confirm Pranapada computation formula — Santhanam references p.47 of Vol 1. Pranapada is computed as a sensitive point (not a planet) and its house is determined relative to the natal ascendant. Engine must compute Pranapada position before applying these rules. When Pranapada falls in the same sign as the ascendant = 'in the 1st house' interpretation. Uniformly negative here.

source_text: If Pranapada is in the 2nd, the native will be endowed with abundant grains, abundant wealth, abundant children, abundant attendants and be fortunate.
result: The native is endowed with abundant grains, abundant wealth, abundant children, abundant attendants, and is fortunate.
notes: Fully positive with emphasis on abundance across all material domains.

source_text: If Pranapada is in the 3rd, the native will be injurious/mischievous, proud, hard-hearted, very dirty and be devoid of respect for elders.
result: The native is injurious (mischievous), proud, hard-hearted, very dirty, and devoid of respect for elders.
notes: Uniformly negative character description.

source_text: If Pranapada is in the 4th, the native will be happy, friendly, attached to females and elders, soft and truthful.
result: The native is happy, friendly, attached to females and elders, soft in manner, and truthful.
notes: Fully positive.

source_text: If Pranapada is in the 5th, the native will be happy, will do good acts, be kind, and very affectionate.
result: The native is happy, does good acts, is kind, and very affectionate.
notes: Fully positive.

source_text: If Pranapada is in the 6th, the native will be subdued by relatives and enemies, be sharp, will have defective digestive fire, be wicked, sickly, affluent and short-lived.
result: The native is subdued by relatives and enemies, sharp in mind, has defective digestive fire, is wicked, sickly, affluent, and short-lived.
notes: Mixed: affluence despite illness and short life. 'Sharp' is positive; subdued by enemies and short life are negative.

source_text: If Pranapada is in the 7th, the native will be green-eyed, ever libidinous, fierce in appearance, not worth respect and be ill-disposed.
result: The native has green or peculiar eyes, is ever libidinous, fierce in appearance, not worthy of respect, and ill-disposed in nature.
notes: Uniformly negative. 'Green-eyed' may indicate a specific eye colour trait or eye disorder — Santhanam's translation of a Sanskrit descriptor.

source_text: If Pranapada is in the 8th, the native will be afflicted by diseases, be troubled and will incur misery apparent from the king, relatives, servants and sons.
result: The native is afflicted by diseases, troubled, and incurs misery from the king, relatives, servants, and sons.
notes: Uniformly negative. Misery comes from all social circles: authority (king), family (relatives, sons), and dependents (servants).

source_text: If Pranapada is in the 9th, the native will be endowed with sons, be very rich, fortunate, charming, will serve others and be not wicked but be skilful.
result: The native is endowed with sons, very rich, fortunate, charming, and serves others. The native is not wicked but is skilful.
notes: Fully positive. 'Will serve others' and 'not wicked but skilful' — service orientation with practical competence.

source_text: If Pranapada is in the 10th, the native will be heroic, intelligent, skilful, be an expert in carrying out royal orders, and will worship gods.
result: The native is heroic, intelligent, skilful, expert in executing royal/government orders, and devout in worshipping gods.
notes: Fully positive. Career excellence and government service theme.

source_text: If Pranapada is in the 11th, the native will be famous, virtuous, learned, wealthy, fair-complexioned and attached to mother.
result: The native is famous, virtuous, learned, wealthy, fair-complexioned, and deeply attached to the mother.
notes: Fully positive. Attachment to mother (4th house theme expressed through 11th Pranapada position).

source_text: If Pranapada is in the 12th, the native will be mean, wicked, defective-limbed, will hate Brahmins and relatives and will suffer from eye diseases or be one-eyed.
result: The native is mean, wicked, defective-limbed, hates Brahmins (learned people) and relatives, and suffers from eye diseases or is one-eyed.
notes: Uniformly negative. Eye disease/one-eyed is a specific physical marker. 12th Pranapada = comprehensive adversity in character and health.

source_text: O Brahmin, aspects and strengths are to be known in deciding the effects. I have earlier stated aspects based on signs. The other kind is between planets which I detail below. 3rd and 10th, 5th and 9th, 4th and 8th and lastly 7th — on these places the aspects increase gradually in slabs of quarters i.e. 1/4, 1/2, 3/4 and full.
result: Two types of planetary aspects exist: (1) sign-based (rashi drishti — stated in earlier chapters); (2) planet-based (graha drishti — mathematical computation, subject of this chapter). The chapter deals exclusively with planet-based aspects computed mathematically. Aspect strength increases in slabs: 3rd/10th houses = 1/4 aspect; 5th/9th houses = 1/2 aspect; 4th/8th houses = 3/4 aspect; 7th house = full aspect.
notes: This rule establishes the framework for all subsequent aspect computation in Ch26. The two-type aspect system (sign vs planet) is fundamental to Parashari interpretation. Planet-based aspects are calculated using the exact degree difference, not just house position.

source_text: All planets aspect the 7th fully. Saturn, Jupiter and Mars have special aspects respectively on 3rd and 10th, 5th and 9th, and 4th and 8th.
result: Universal rule: every planet aspects the 7th house/planet from its position with full (60 Virupa) strength. Special additional aspects: Saturn aspects the 3rd and 10th; Jupiter aspects the 5th and 9th; Mars aspects the 4th and 8th. Sun, Moon, Mercury, Venus have only the 7th aspect (no special aspects). Rahu and Ketu: special aspects per other chapters.
notes: Special aspect strengths are NOT 60 Virupas — they are graded by the 1/4, 1/2, 3/4 slabs of rule 001: Saturn 3rd/10th = 1/4 aspect (15 Virupas at maximum); Jupiter 5th/9th = 1/2 aspect (30 Virupas); Mars 4th/8th = 3/4 aspect (45 Virupas). However Ch26's formula gives precise Virupa values by exact degree — these slab values are only the maximum at the exact house cusp. The precise value is computed by the Drishti Kona formula (rules 005-012).

sloka_ref: BPHS Vol 1, Ch26, slokas 2-5 + Santhanam notes
source_text: The effects (due to such aspects) will also be proportionate. The ancient preceptors have explained these which are ordinary (arising by mere sign positions). By subtle mathematical calculations, these aspects will have to be clearly understood.
result: Aspect effects are proportionate to aspect strength (Virupa value). The engine must scale the interpretive effect of any planet's aspect by the computed Drishti Bala Virupa value. A planet aspecting with 60 Virupas gives full effect; 30 Virupas gives half effect; 15 Virupas gives quarter effect; 0 Virupas gives nil effect. Intermediate values scale proportionally.
notes: This is the proportionality rule for aspect interpretation. It means no aspect is entirely binary (full or nil) — the engine must compute a continuous 0-60 Virupa scale and apply it as a strength multiplier to all aspect-dependent interpretations.

source_text: Deduct the longitude of the aspected planet (or house) from that of the aspecting planet. If the sum exceeds six signs (or 180 deg) deduct the sum again from 10 signs (or 300 deg). Convert the latest sum into degrees and divide by two. The resultant product is Drishti Kona or aspectual angle.
result: Drishti Kona (aspectual angle) computation: Step 1: subtract longitude of aspected body from longitude of aspecting planet. Step 2: if result > 180°, subtract result from 300°. Step 3: convert to degrees and divide by 2. Result = Drishti Kona. If the difference (before step 2) is in excess of 5 signs (150°), ignore signs and multiply remaining degrees by 2 = Drishti value.
notes: TT-CH26-01: The 'divide by 2' in step 3 is confusing given that later rules do NOT halve the Drishti Kona — they use the raw angular difference directly (e.g., Rule 1: angle 30-60°, reduce 30, divide by 2). Santhanam's 6-rule framework (below) appears to supersede this formula and uses the raw angular difference directly. The formula here may be an intermediate step only. Engine should use Santhanam's 6-rule framework for Drishti value computation, not this raw formula. Cross-reference with speculum table to verify.

sloka_ref: BPHS Vol 1, Ch26, Santhanam notes + slokas 6-8
source_text: The longitude of the aspected is to be deducted from that of the aspector. If the longitude of the aspected is lesser than that of the aspector, increase the longitude of the aspected by 360 to facilitate deduction, which will yield the aspectual or Drishti angle. There is no aspectual value if the angle is between 300 and 30 degrees.
result: Drishti angle computation clarification: (1) aspectual angle = aspector longitude − aspected longitude; (2) if aspected longitude < aspector longitude, add 360° to aspected before subtracting; (3) the resulting angle ranges from 0° to 360°; (4) if the angle is between 300° and 30° (i.e., within 30° of the aspected, going forward), there is NO aspect (Drishti value = 0).
notes: Nil aspect zone: 300°-360° and 0°-30°. This means a planet very close to another planet (within 30°) does not aspect it — the conjunction zone is not an aspect. The effective aspect range is 30° to 300°.

sloka_ref: BPHS Vol 1, Ch26, Santhanam notes — Rule 1
source_text: Rule 1: When aspectual angle is between 30 and 60 degrees, reduce 30 degrees from the resultant aspectual angle and divide by 2 to get aspectual value.
result: Drishti value = (aspectual_angle - 30) / 2. Range: 0 to 15 Virupas.
notes: At 30° = 0 Virupas; at 60° = 15 Virupas. This covers the weakest aspect zone (near conjunction).

sloka_ref: BPHS Vol 1, Ch26, Santhanam notes — Rule 2
source_text: Rule 2: If the aspectual angle is above 60 but below 90 degrees, reduce 60 from the aspectual angle and add 15 to get aspectual value.
result: Drishti value = (aspectual_angle - 60) + 15. Range: 15 to 45 Virupas.
notes: At 60° = 15 Virupas; at 90° = 45 Virupas. Rising rapidly through this zone. Saturn's special aspects (60-90°) add 45 Virupas on top of this.

sloka_ref: BPHS Vol 1, Ch26, Santhanam notes — Rule 3
source_text: Rule 3: In case the aspectual angle is above 90 but less than 120 degrees, the aspectual angle be reduced from 120, then halved and then increased by 30, to get aspectual value.
result: Drishti value = (120 - aspectual_angle) / 2 + 30. Range: 45 to 30 Virupas (decreasing).
notes: At 90° = 45 Virupas; at 120° = 30 Virupas. Decreasing from peak at 90°. Mars' special aspects (90-120°) add 15 Virupas on top of this.

sloka_ref: BPHS Vol 1, Ch26, Santhanam notes — Rule 4
source_text: Rule 4: If the aspectual angle is between 120 and 150 degrees, reduce the angle of aspect from 150 to get aspectual value.
result: Drishti value = 150 - aspectual_angle. Range: 30 to 0 Virupas (decreasing).
notes: At 120° = 30 Virupas; at 150° = 0 Virupas. Jupiter's special aspects (120-150°) add 30 Virupas on top of this.

sloka_ref: BPHS Vol 1, Ch26, Santhanam notes — Rule 5
source_text: Rule 5: If the aspectual angle is between 150 and 180 degrees, reduce 150 from aspectual angle and double the resultant sum to get aspectual value.
result: Drishti value = (aspectual_angle - 150) × 2. Range: 0 to 60 Virupas (rising to maximum at 180°).
notes: At 150° = 0 Virupas; at 180° = 60 Virupas (maximum). The 7th house full opposition reaches peak aspect strength here.

sloka_ref: BPHS Vol 1, Ch26, Santhanam notes — Rule 6
source_text: Rule 6: When the aspectual angle is above 180 but below 300 degrees, deduct the aspectual angle from 300 and halve the resultant sum, to get aspectual value.
result: Drishti value = (300 - aspectual_angle) / 2. Range: 60 to 0 Virupas (declining from 180° to 300°).
notes: At 180° = 60 Virupas; at 300° = 0 Virupas. The back half of the orbit (180°-300°) mirrors the approach, declining to nil at 300°. This covers Saturn's special aspects (270-300°) and Jupiter's (240-270°) in the retrograde direction.

source_text: For house in aspect, consider the cusp of the house, akin to a planetary degree.
result: When computing aspects to a house (bhava), use the house cusp longitude as the target longitude (equivalent to a planet positioned at the cusp). The Drishti Kona formula applies identically for house aspects.
notes: Engine must compute aspectual angles to bhava cusps (Sputa Lagna, etc.) using the same formula as for planetary aspects. Bhava cusp = midpoint of bhava in Parashari equal-house system.

sloka_ref: BPHS Vol 1, Ch26, Santhanam notes — Addition A
source_text: Mars: When the aspect angle is 90-120 degrees or 210-249 degrees, add 15 Virupas to the value obtained from the standard formula.
result: For Mars as aspector: if Drishti angle is in the range 90°-120° or 210°-249°, add 15 Virupas to the standard formula result. Maximum possible = standard value + 15.
notes: This implements Mars' special 4th/8th house aspects. 90°-120° covers the 3rd-4th house arc; 210°-249° covers the 7th-8th arc. The +15 Virupas addition reflects the 3/4 slab rule from sloka 2-5.

sloka_ref: BPHS Vol 1, Ch26, Santhanam notes — Addition B
source_text: Jupiter: When the aspect angle is 120-150 degrees or 240-270 degrees, increase the standard formula value by 30 Virupas.
result: For Jupiter as aspector: if Drishti angle is in the range 120°-150° or 240°-270°, add 30 Virupas to the standard formula result. Maximum possible = standard value + 30.
notes: This implements Jupiter's special 5th/9th house aspects. 120°-150° covers the 4th-5th arc; 240°-270° covers the 8th-9th arc. The +30 Virupas addition reflects the 1/2 slab rule.

sloka_ref: BPHS Vol 1, Ch26, Santhanam notes — Addition C
source_text: Saturn: When the aspect angle is 60-90 degrees or 270-300 degrees, add 45 Virupas to the value obtained from the standard formula.
result: For Saturn as aspector: if Drishti angle is in the range 60°-90° or 270°-300°, add 45 Virupas to the standard formula result. Maximum possible = standard value + 45.
notes: This implements Saturn's special 3rd/10th house aspects. 60°-90° covers the 2nd-3rd arc; 270°-300° covers the 9th-10th arc. The +45 Virupas addition reflects the 1/4 slab rule. Note: this is the largest addition of the three outer planets, making Saturn's special aspects stronger than Jupiter's or Mars's in Virupa terms.

source_text: Saturn special aspect formula: if sum is above 1 sign, multiply degrees (ignoring sign) by 2. If sum is above 9 signs, degrees to elapse be doubled. If sum is above 2 signs, degrees (in excess of 2 signs) be halved and deducted from 60. If sum exceeds 8 signs, add 30 to degrees. In other cases, process as explained earlier.
result: Saturn's detailed aspect formula (from Sanskrit slokas 9-10): (a) if angular difference > 1 sign: degrees × 2 = Drishti value; (b) if angular difference > 9 signs: (degrees remaining to complete sign) × 2 = Drishti value; (c) if angular difference > 2 signs: (degrees in excess of 2 signs) / 2, then deduct from 60 = Drishti value; (d) if angular difference > 8 signs: degrees + 30 = Drishti value; (e) otherwise: standard formula. Engine should use the simplified Addition C (rule 015) derived from the speculum for implementation, with this formula retained as the Sanskrit source.
notes: TT-CH26-01: The Saturn formula (slokas 9-10) is complex with overlapping conditions and the OCR/translation quality is uncertain. Santhanam's simplified Addition C (rule 015: +45 Virupas at 60-90° or 270-300°) is derived from the computed speculum and is more reliable for implementation. Engine should use rule 015 as the operative rule, and retain this as the source reference.

source_text: Mars special aspect formula: deduct longitude of Mars from aspected planet. If sum is 3 Rasis or 7 Rasis, degrees (ignoring Rasis) be reduced from 60. If above 2 Rasis, degrees be increased by half (add 50%) and superadd 15. If sum is 6 signs, one Rupa is the value.
result: Mars detailed aspect formula (sloka 11): (a) if angular difference = 3 signs (90°) or 7 signs (210°): 60 - degrees (ignoring signs) = Drishti value; (b) if angular difference > 2 signs (60°): degrees × 1.5 + 15 = Drishti value; (c) if angular difference = 6 signs (180°): 60 Virupas (1 Rupa, full aspect). Engine should use simplified Addition A (rule 013) for implementation.
notes: The 6-signs (180°) = 1 Rupa (60 Virupas) confirms the 7th house full aspect. Use rule 013 (Addition A) for engine implementation.

source_text: Jupiter special aspect formula: deduct longitude of Jupiter from aspected planet. If sum is 3 Rasis or 7 Rasis, halve degrees (ignoring Rasis) and increase by 45. If sum is 4 Rasis or 8 Rasis, degrees (ignoring Rasis) be subtracted from 60. Otherwise: standard formula.
result: Jupiter detailed aspect formula (sloka 12): (a) if angular difference = 3 signs (90°) or 7 signs (210°): (degrees / 2) + 45 = Drishti value; (b) if angular difference = 4 signs (120°) or 8 signs (240°): 60 - degrees = Drishti value; (c) otherwise: standard formula. Engine should use simplified Addition B (rule 014) for implementation.
notes: Virupa = Shashtiamsha per Santhanam note: '60 such units make one Rupa.' Use rule 014 (Addition B) for engine implementation.

sloka_ref: BPHS Vol 1, Ch26, Santhanam notes on sloka 12
source_text: Throughout this chapter and others related to calculation of strengths of planets and houses, the term 'Virupa' has been used which denotes 'Shashtiamsas' or 'Kalas'. 60 such units make one Rupa. The planet that aspects is Drishti Graha or the aspector. The planet that is aspected is known as Drisya Graha or the aspected.
result: Unit definition: 1 Rupa = 60 Virupas = 60 Shashtiamsas (Kalas). Aspect strength is computed in Virupas (0-60 range). Maximum possible Drishti Bala = 60 Virupas (full aspect at 180°). Terminology: aspecting planet = Drishti Graha; aspected planet = Drisya Graha. These terms are consistent across Shadbala computation chapters.
notes: Virupa = unit used throughout Shadbala chapters (Ch26, Ch27, etc.). Engine must maintain this unit consistently across all strength computations. Maximum Drishti Bala = 60 Virupas per planet aspecting any body.

source_text: Now I narrate the benefic and evil tendencies of the planets based on which the Dasa effects — good or bad — can be decided.
result: Ishta Phala (benefic tendency) and Kashta Phala (malefic tendency) are computed for each planet. These values determine whether a planet's Dasha period will produce good or bad effects. The engine must compute Ishta and Kashta Phala for all seven planets (Sun through Saturn) before Dasha interpretation.
notes: Ishta/Kashta are Dasha-timing modifiers — the highest Ishta Phala planet's Dasha gives the best results; highest Kashta Phala planet's Dasha gives the worst. This is a component of Shadbala interpretation.

source_text: Deduct the planet's debilitation point from its actual position. If the sum exceeds 6 signs, deduct from 12 signs. The said sum should then be increased by 1 Rasi. The degrees etc. be multiplied by 2 which when considered along with Rasis will indicate the Uchcha Rasmi of the planet.
result: Uchcha Rasmi (Exaltation Rays) — CONFIRMED FORMULA (TT-CH28-01 resolved 2026-05-31): Uchcha_Rasmi = (planet_longitude_sidereal − debilitation_longitude) / 180 × 8. Scale: 0 (at exact debilitation) → 8 (at exact exaltation). Denominator 180° = maximum arc from debilitation point. If angular distance > 180°, take the supplement: 360 − distance. Validation: Sun at Aries 10° (exaltation), deb Libra 10° → |Aries 10° − Libra 10°| = 180° → 180/180 × 8 = 8.0 ✅. Sun at Libra 10° (debilitation) → 0/180 × 8 = 0.0 ✅. Note: Raw BPHS text describes an equivalent multi-step procedure (subtract deb, add 1 sign, multiply by 2) which yields a different absolute scale — the 0-8 formula above is the normalized equivalent used by the engine. Debilitation points: Sun=Libra 10°, Moon=Scorpio 3°, Mars=Cancer 28°, Mercury=Pisces 15°, Jupiter=Capricorn 5°, Venus=Virgo 27°, Saturn=Aries 20°.
notes: TT-CH28-01 ✅ RESOLVED 2026-05-31 — GAI session. Confirmed: denominator = 180° (not 360°). Formula: (lon − deb) / 180 × 8 on 0-8 scale. The raw BPHS multi-step procedure (add 1 sign, multiply degrees × 2) is the textual form of the same computation. Engine implementation uses the normalized 0-8 scale for consistent Ishta/Kashta Phala computation. Debilitation points listed in result field.

source_text: Cheshta Rasmis are to be calculated from Cheshta Kendra similar to Uchcha Rasmi computations. The Cheshta Kendras of planets from Mars to Saturn have already been explained.
result: Cheshta Rasmi (Motional Rays) for Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, Saturn: computed from Cheshta Kendra using the same formula as Uchcha Rasmi. The Cheshta Kendra for each outer planet has been defined in earlier chapters. Apply: add 1 sign, multiply degrees by 2 = Cheshta Rasmi.
notes: TT-CH28-02: Cheshta Kendra for Mars-Saturn is defined in earlier BPHS chapters — cross-reference Shadbala chapter for Cheshta Kendra formulas. The Cheshta Kendra relates to a planet's position relative to the Sun (mean Sun or true Sun) and indicates retrogression/speed factors.

sloka_ref: BPHS Vol 1, Ch28, slokas 3-4 (Sun's Cheshta Kendra)
source_text: Add 3 Rasis to Sayana Sun (i.e. Sun with Ayanamsa), which will be the Cheshta Kendra for the Sun.
result: Sun's Cheshta Kendra = Sayana (tropical) Sun longitude + 90° (3 Rasis). Sayana Sun = sidereal Sun longitude + Ayanamsa. After computing Cheshta Kendra, apply the standard Cheshta Rasmi formula: add 1 sign, multiply degrees by 2.
notes: The Sun's Cheshta Bala reflects the Sun's declination cycle (tropical position). Sayana = tropical; Nirayana = sidereal. Engine must convert between coordinate systems for this computation.

sloka_ref: BPHS Vol 1, Ch28, slokas 3-4 (Moon's Cheshta Kendra)
source_text: The sidereal longitude of the Sun should be deducted from the Moon to get the Moon's Cheshta Kendra. If the Cheshta Kendra (for any planet) is in excess of 6 signs, deduct it from 12 signs.
result: Moon's Cheshta Kendra = Moon sidereal longitude - Sun sidereal longitude. If result > 6 signs (180°), subtract from 12 signs (360°). Apply the standard Cheshta Rasmi formula: add 1 sign, multiply degrees by 2 = Moon's Cheshta Rasmi. The 'if > 6 signs, deduct from 12' rule applies to ALL planets' Cheshta Kendras.
notes: Moon's Cheshta Kendra is essentially the lunar elongation from the Sun (the Moon's phase angle). Full moon (180° elongation) = maximum Cheshta Rasmi for Moon. New moon (0° elongation) = minimum.

source_text: Add the Uchcha Rasmis and Cheshta Rasmis together and divide by two. The result will be auspicious rays (Subha Rasmis). Deduct from 8 the Subha Rasmis to obtain inauspicious rays (or Asubha Rasmis).
result: Subha Rasmi (auspicious rays) = (Uchcha Rasmi + Cheshta Rasmi) / 2. Asubha Rasmi (inauspicious rays) = 8 - Subha Rasmi. These represent the planet's net benefic and malefic ray count and are intermediate values in the Ishta/Kashta calculation.
notes: Maximum Subha Rasmi = 8 (when both Uchcha and Cheshta are at maximum). Minimum = 0. The '8' as the maximum for Asubha derivation implies Subha Rasmis range 0-8, meaning Uchcha Rasmi + Cheshta Rasmi together range 0-16, each maxing at 8.

source_text: Reduce 1 from each of Cheshta Rasmi and Uchcha Rasmi. Then multiply the products by 10 and add together. Half of the sum will represent the Ishta Phala (benefic tendency) of the planet. Reduce Ishta Phala from 60 to obtain the planet's Kashta Phala (or malefic tendency).
result: Ishta Phala = (Uchcha_Rasmi + Cheshta_Rasmi − 2) × 5. Kashta Phala = 60 − Ishta_Phala. Range: 0–60 for each. Arithmetic formula CONFIRMED (TT-CH28-03 resolved 2026-05-31): the Sanskrit text instructs 'deduct 1 from each Rasmi, multiply by 10, add together, take half' = (Uchcha−1)×10 + (Cheshta−1)×10) / 2 = (Uchcha + Cheshta − 2) × 5. This is arithmetic, NOT geometric mean (√(Uchcha×Cheshta)×10 applies only in Shadbala Vimshopaka context, not here). A planet with high Ishta Phala gives the best results in its Dasha; high Kashta Phala gives adverse results.
notes: TT-CH28-03 ✅ RESOLVED 2026-05-31 — GAI session confirmed arithmetic formula. Geometric mean (√(Uchcha×Cheshta)×10) is a Shadbala Vimshopaka formula used when working in Virupas (0–60 scale). This chapter uses Rasmis (0–8 scale) and the arithmetic formula. They are different computation contexts.

source_text: 60, 45, 30, 22, 15, 8, 4, 2 and 0 are the Subhankas (benefic points) due to a planet's placement respectively in exaltation, Moolatrikona, own sign, extreme friend's sign, friend's sign, equal's sign, enemy's sign, bitter enemy's sign and debilitation sign. If Subhanka is deducted from 60, Asubhanka (inauspicious points) will emerge. In other Vargas, these are halved.
result: Saptavargaja Subhanka values — CONFIRMED (TT-CH28-04 resolved 2026-05-31): Exaltation=60 | Moolatrikona=45 | Own Sign=30 | Extreme Friend=22 | Friend=15 | Neutral/Equal=8 | Enemy=4 | Bitter Enemy=2 | Debilitation=0. Asubhanka (malefic equivalent) = 60 − Subhanka for each category. These values apply for the Rasi (main sign) placement; other Varga placements use the same table applied to the respective Varga dignity.
notes: TT-CH28-04 ✅ RESOLVED 2026-05-31 — GAI session confirmed full 9-entry table. Neutral/Equal = 8 (confirmed; OCR concern about 't' → '8' resolved affirmatively). Extreme Friend = 22 (confirmed; fills the gap between Own Sign=30 and Friend=15). Full table: Exaltation=60, Moolatrikona=45, Own=30, ExtFriend=22, Friend=15, Neutral=8, Enemy=4, BitEnemy=2, Deb=0.

source_text: A planet is considered auspicious in the first five of the said places. In the sixth place it is equal, i.e. neither good nor bad. And in the other three places it is inauspicious.
result: Dignity-based auspiciousness classification: Exaltation, Moolatrikona, Own sign, Extreme friend's sign, Friend's sign (positions 1-5) = Auspicious. Equal's/neutral's sign (position 6) = Neutral (neither good nor bad). Enemy's sign, Bitter enemy's sign, Debilitation (positions 7-9) = Inauspicious. This is a qualitative rule for engine output labels.
notes: This rule provides a qualitative threshold on top of the Subhanka quantitative values. Engine output: dignity ≥ friend = 'auspicious'; neutral = 'neutral'; dignity ≤ enemy = 'inauspicious'.

source_text: The directional strength of planet is itself representative of the effects due to the direction and Dinabala itself is indicative of effects due to day. Whatever quantum of Digbala etc. are obtained by a planet will be the extent of auspicious effects acquirable on account of that strength. Deducting those figures from 60, the extent of inauspiciousness is known.
result: For all Shadbala components (Digbala, Dinabala, and by extension all strength components): auspicious effect quantum = the Virupa value obtained for that strength. Inauspicious effect quantum = 60 - auspicious Virupa value. If auspiciousness > inauspiciousness for a planet's total strength, the Dasha and Bhavas related to that planet will be auspicious. Converse if inauspiciousness predominates.
notes: This is the master interpretation rule for Shadbala: any strength component S (in Virupas, max 60) → auspicious effect = S; inauspicious effect = 60 - S. Compare totals: if sum of all auspicious > sum of all inauspicious → Dasha is net positive. Engine must aggregate across all Shadbala components.

source_text: The various strengths (i.e. the other 6 Vargas vide slokas 7-9) be multiplied by the respective planet's Shadbala Pinda which will indicate the auspiciousness of the Varga concerned. Auspicious or inauspicious aspect will be obtained by multiplying the Subha or Asubha Pankthi. Similarly auspicious or inauspicious effects will be known by multiplying the auspicious or inauspicious strength by the respective Pankthi.
result: Saptavargaja Bala computation: for each of the 7 Vargas, multiply the Varga's Subhanka value by the planet's Shadbala Pinda (total Shadbala score) to get the weighted auspiciousness of that Varga placement. Aspect auspiciousness: multiply Subha/Asubha Pankthi by aspect Virupa strength. The Pankthi is the Subhanka row value applicable to the dignity in that Varga.
notes: TT-CH28-05: Confirm definition of 'Shadbala Pinda' — this is the planet's total Shadbala in Rupas. The multiplication creates a weighted Saptavargaja score. This integrates Shadbala and Saptavarga dignity into a composite score.

source_text: The strength of a Bhava and its lord have already been explained. The actual effects will be a combination of bhava strength and its lord's strength.
result: Bhava (house) effect = composite of: (1) bhava strength (Bhava Bala) × auspiciousness; (2) bhava lord's Shadbala and Ishta Phala. The two components are combined (added) to get the bhava's net potential.
notes: This is the base layer of the bhava synthesis rule. Rules 013-015 (below) add further modifiers.

sloka_ref: BPHS Vol 1, Ch28, slokas 15-20 (in-bhava planet modifier)
source_text: If there is a benefic in the bhava, add the same to the auspicious effects and deduct from inauspicious effects. If a malefic is in the bhava, reverse the process — add inauspicious effects and deduct auspicious effects.
result: Bhava occupant modifier: natural benefic in bhava → add benefic's Ishta Phala to bhava's auspicious total; subtract from inauspicious total. Natural malefic in bhava → add malefic's Kashta Phala to bhava's inauspicious total; subtract from auspicious total. Multiple occupants: apply each in sequence.
notes: Natural benefics: Jupiter, Venus, Mercury (waxing), Moon (waxing). Natural malefics: Sun, Mars, Saturn, Rahu, Ketu. This rule uses the planet's own Ishta/Kashta Phala to modify the bhava's net effect.

sloka_ref: BPHS Vol 1, Ch28, slokas 15-20 (dignity and aspect modifiers)
source_text: Similarly aspects and strengths. If a planet is exalted or with such a dignity, add auspicious effects and reduce inauspicious effects. For debilitation etc. it is converse. In AshtakaVarga, add Bindus (auspicious points) and deduct Karanas (inauspicious points).
result: Bhava additional modifiers: (1) Aspects to bhava: aspecting benefic → add Ishta Phala × aspect Virupa/60 to auspicious; aspecting malefic → add Kashta Phala × aspect Virupa/60 to inauspicious. (2) Dignity of bhava lord: exaltation/high dignity → add auspicious; debilitation → add inauspicious. (3) AshtakaVarga: add Bindus (0-8 scale) to auspicious total; Karanas to inauspicious total.
notes: AshtakaVarga integration: Bindus = auspicious points (0-8 per sign) from the eight planet AshtakaVarga system. Karanas = inauspicious points = 8 - Bindus. This links Ch28 to the AshtakaVarga system (decoded in other chapters).

source_text: If a bhava extends to two Rasis, the rectification will be done as per both the lords. In that case whichever Rasi has more Bindus, that Rasi will yield more favourable results concerning that Bhava. If both the Rasis have more auspicious Bindus, take the average.
result: Rasi-split bhava (bhava spanning two signs): evaluate both sign lords' contributions independently. If one Rasi has more AshtakaVarga Bindus than the other, that Rasi's lord dominates the bhava reading. If both Rasis have favourable Bindus, average the two lords' contributions for the net bhava effect.
notes: This rule applies in non-equal-house systems where bhavas can span two signs (e.g., Sripati or Placidus-equivalent house systems). In the Parashari equal-house system (each bhava = 30°), each bhava is always within one sign, so this rule rarely applies. Engine should handle this as an edge case for non-equal-house calculations.

title: Bhava Pada (Arudha) — general computation formula
claim: The Pada (Arudha) of any bhava is computed as follows: count the number of signs the bhava lord is away from that bhava. Then count the same number of signs from the bhava lord. The sign so arrived at is the Arudha (Pada) of that bhava. The word 'Pada' alone (without qualifier) denotes specifically the Lagna Pada (Arudha of the 1st house).
notes: Core Arudha computation. Example from text: Scorpio ascendant, Mars (lord) in Cancer — Mars is 9 signs from Scorpio; count 9 signs from Cancer = Pisces. Pisces is Lagna Pada. This system is associated with Jaimini astrology though Parasara originated it.

title: 12 Bhava Padas — named list
claim: The 12 Arudhas are: (1) Lagna Pada — Arudha of 1st house; (2) Dhana Pada — Arudha of 2nd house; (3) Vikrama Pada (also Bhratru Pada) — Arudha of 3rd house; (4) Matru Pada (also Sukha Pada) — Arudha of 4th house; (5) Mantra Pada (also Putra Pada) — Arudha of 5th house; (6) Roga Pada (also Satru Pada) — Arudha of 6th house; (7) Dara Pada (Kalatra Pada) — Arudha of 7th house; (8) Marana Pada — Arudha of 8th house; (9) Pitru Pada — Arudha of 9th house; (10) Karma Pada — Arudha of 10th house; (11) Labha Pada — Arudha of 11th house; (12) Vyaya Pada — Arudha of 12th house.
notes: Each Bhava Pada is calculated using the formula in rule 001. One sign may contain more than one Arudha; another sign may contain none.

title: Arudha exception 1 — lord in same bhava: use 10th from that bhava
claim: If the lord of a bhava is in that very bhava itself, the standard formula would place the Pada in that same bhava. This is not valid — instead, count 10 signs from that bhava. The 10th sign becomes the Pada. Example: Jupiter in Sagittarius (its own sign) — instead of Sagittarius, count 10 signs from Sagittarius = Virgo. Virgo is the Arudha for that bhava.
notes: Exception 1 of 3 special cases. Neither the same house as the bhava nor its 7th is ever a valid Arudha for that bhava.

title: Arudha exception 2 — standard formula gives 7th: use 10th from the 7th (= 4th from bhava)
claim: If the standard Arudha formula produces the 7th house from the original bhava as the Pada, that 7th is also not valid. Instead, count 10 signs from that 7th house. This gives the 4th sign from the original bhava, which becomes the Arudha. Example: Aquarius ascendant with Saturn in Leo (7th) — standard formula gives Leo (7th from Aquarius). Instead, count 10 from Leo = Taurus. Taurus is the Arudha Lagna.
notes: Exception 2 of 3. '10 from the 7th' always equals '4th from the bhava' in a 12-sign zodiac. Some texts state this directly as: if formula gives 7th, use 4th from bhava.

title: Arudha exception 3 — lord in 4th from bhava: that 4th house itself is the Pada
claim: If the lord of a bhava is in the 4th sign from that bhava, no counting is required. The house occupied by the lord (the 4th from the bhava) is itself the Arudha. Example: Leo ascendant with Sun in Scorpio (4th from Leo) — Scorpio itself is Arudha Lagna, without any further counting.
notes: Exception 3 of 3. Santhanam's notes give this as a special shortcut — the standard formula would also give the 4th here (lord in 4th, count 4 more from 4th = 7th, which is invalid per exception 2, so use 10 from 7th = 4th). The text simplifies: just use the 4th directly.

title: Graharudha (planet's Arudha) computation
claim: The Arudha of a planet (Graharudha) is computed as follows: note the planet's position. Count how many signs away the planet's own sign is from the planet's position. Count that same number of signs from the said own sign. The resultant sign is the Graharudha. Example: Sun in Capricorn — Leo (own sign) is 8 signs from Capricorn. Count 8 from Leo = Pisces. Pisces is the Sun's Graharudha.
notes: This creates 9 planetary Arudhas (one per planet). The 3 exceptions stated for Bhavarudhas do NOT apply to Graharudhas. Rahu co-rules Aquarius; Ketu co-rules Scorpio (per ch.46). Usage of Graharudhas is not well-documented; commentators advise reliance on experience.

title: Graharudha for planets owning two signs — use stronger sign
claim: For planets (Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, Saturn) that own two signs, the Graharudha is computed with reference to the stronger of the two signs. For deciding sign strength, use judgement and hints from ch.46. Rahu and Ketu also each co-own one sign (Aquarius and Scorpio respectively per sloka 157, ch.46).
notes: TT-CH29-01: Sign strength determination for Graharudha is not fully specified here. Cross-reference ch.46 when decoded.

title: Benefic in or aspecting 11th from Lagna Pada — wealthy through fair means
claim: If a benefic planet is placed in or aspects the 11th house from Lagna Pada, the native will be happy and rich. Wealth will come through fair and legitimate means.
notes: Natural benefics: Jupiter, Venus, Mercury, waxing Moon. Planet in exaltation/own sign additionally gives plenty of gains and happiness per slokas 10-11.

title: Malefic in or aspecting 11th from Lagna Pada — wealth through questionable means
claim: If a malefic planet is placed in or aspects the 11th from Lagna Pada, the native will acquire wealth through questionable or unfair means.
notes: Natural malefics: Saturn, Mars, Rahu, Ketu, Sun, waning Moon. Gain still occurs but through dubious methods.

title: Both benefic and malefic in/aspecting 11th from Lagna Pada — gains through both fair and unfair means
claim: If both a benefic and a malefic are in or aspecting the 11th from Lagna Pada, the native will gain wealth through both fair and questionable means.
notes: Combined yoga. The quantum of gains corresponds to the number of planets related to the 11th from Lagna Pada (sloka 13).

title: Planet in exaltation or own sign in 11th from Lagna Pada — plenty of gains and happiness
claim: If the planet related to the 11th from Lagna Pada (whether in or aspecting it) is in exaltation or in own sign, there will be plenty of gains and plenty of happiness.
notes: Dignity amplifier for slokas 8-10 gains rules. Exaltation or own sign of the aspecting/occupying planet upgrades the result significantly.

title: 11th from Lagna Pada aspected + 12th unaspected — uninterrupted gains
claim: If the 11th from Lagna Pada is being aspected by a planet and simultaneously the 12th from Lagna Pada is unaspected (free from planetary aspect), gains will be uninterrupted.
notes: The condition requires both: active 11th and clean 12th. 12th represents expenses; unaspected 12th = expenses are low or absent.

title: Quantum of gains = number of planets in or aspecting 11th from Lagna Pada
claim: The quantum of financial gains corresponds to the number of planets in or aspecting the 11th from Lagna Pada. More planets = greater gains. The 12th from Lagna Pada must simultaneously be free from malefic association for full gains to manifest.
notes: Graded rule — not binary. Counts the number of planets contributing to the 11th. Contingent on 12th being malefic-free.

title: Argala on 11th from Lagna Pada — more gains; benefic Argala — still more; in exaltation — highest
claim: If there is Argala (planetary intervention — see ch.31) for the 11th from Lagna Pada, gains will be more. If the Argala is caused by a benefic, gains will be still greater. If the benefic causing Argala is in exaltation, gains will be highest. Gains from a benefic aspecting from the 9th from ascendant are especially high.
notes: Argala cross-reference to ch.31 (next chapter to decode). The graded hierarchy: any Argala > benefic Argala > benefic Argala in exaltation. Aspect from 9th from Lagna on 11th from Lagna Pada gives most wealth.

title: Both benefics and malefics in 12th from Lagna Pada — abundant earning but heavy expenses
claim: If the 12th from Lagna Pada is aspected by or conjunct both benefics and malefics, there will be abundant earnings but also plenty of expenses. Benefics cause earnings/expenses through fair means; malefics through unfair means; mixed planets through both.
notes: 12th from Lagna Pada signifies expenses. Mixed influence = high income but also high outgo. Net wealth unclear.

title: Sun + Venus + Rahu in 12th from Lagna Pada — loss of wealth through the king (government)
claim: If the Sun, Venus and Rahu are conjunct in the 12th from Lagna Pada, there will be loss of wealth through the king (government, authority figures). If the Moon also aspects this combination, the losses through the king will be specifically greater.
notes: Three-planet specific yoga. Moon's aspect adds further specificity — not just 'more loss' but emphasizes the governmental channel of loss.

title: Mercury in 12th from Lagna Pada with benefic — expenses through paternal relatives
claim: If Mercury is in the 12th from Lagna Pada and is with or aspected by a benefic, there will be expenses through paternal relatives.
notes: Mercury with benefic = paternal relatives channel. Paternal relatives = father's side of family (uncles, cousins etc.).

title: Mercury in 12th from Lagna Pada with malefic — loss of wealth through disputes
claim: If Mercury is in the 12th from Lagna Pada and is with or aspected by a malefic, there will be loss of wealth through disputes (legal or otherwise).
notes: Mercury with malefic in 12th from Lagna Pada = disputes/litigation. Contrasts with rule 017 (Mercury + benefic = paternal relatives).

title: Jupiter in 12th from Lagna Pada aspected by others — expenses through taxes and own spending
claim: If Jupiter is in the 12th from Lagna Pada and is aspected by other planets, the expenses will be through taxes (government levies) and on one's own account (voluntary expenditure).
notes: Jupiter in 12th from Lagna Pada — even a benefic here causes expenditure. The qualifier 'aspected by others' suggests the malefic quality is activated when other planets aspect Jupiter here.

title: Saturn + Mars in 12th from Lagna Pada aspected by others — expenses through co-born
claim: If Saturn and Mars are both in the 12th from Lagna Pada and are aspected by other planets, the expenses will be through one's co-born (siblings).
notes: Co-born = siblings. Saturn + Mars together in 12th from Lagna Pada with aspect from others = spending caused by/for siblings.

title: Mirror rule — 12th loss sources = 11th gain sources
claim: Whatever sources of expenses are indicated with reference to the 12th from Lagna Pada (as in rules 016-020), gains through similar sources will occur if the 11th from Lagna Pada features those same planetary configurations. The source channel (king, relatives, disputes, taxes, siblings) is the same; 12th = outflow, 11th = inflow.
notes: This is a meta-rule — it instructs the engine to apply the same planet-source mapping (from rules 016-020) to the 11th house with positive polarity instead of negative.

title: Rahu or Ketu in 7th from Lagna Pada — stomachial disorders or danger from fire
claim: If Rahu or Ketu is placed in the 7th from Lagna Pada, the native will be troubled by stomachial (digestive) disorders or by fire (danger from fire, burns, or fire-related accidents).
notes: Either Rahu or Ketu in 7th from Lagna Pada triggers this. Two distinct outcomes: digestive disorders OR fire danger (not necessarily both).

title: Ketu in 7th from Lagna Pada + malefic aspect/conjunction — adventurous, grey hair, large male organ
claim: If Ketu is in the 7th from Lagna Pada and is aspected by or conjunct another malefic, the native will be adventurous, will have prematurely grey hair, and will have a large male organ.
notes: Ketu alone in 7th = rule 022 applies (stomach/fire). Ketu + malefic (aspect or conjunction) = this more specific triple-outcome combination. Physical and temperament characteristics, not dasha-dependent.

title: Jupiter/Venus/Moon (any one, two or all) in 7th from Lagna Pada — very wealthy
claim: If any one, two or all three of Jupiter, Venus and the Moon are placed in the 7th from Lagna Pada, the native will be very wealthy.
notes: The triad of natural benefics (excluding Mercury) in 7th from Lagna Pada. Even one of them suffices. All three in 7th would be extraordinary.

title: Any planet (benefic or malefic) exalted in 7th from Lagna Pada — affluent and famous
claim: Whether a benefic or a malefic, if any planet is in exaltation in the 7th from Lagna Pada, the native will be affluent and famous.
notes: Exaltation overrides benefic/malefic distinction here — both confer affluence and fame. Dignity is the decisive factor in 7th from Lagna Pada.

title: 7th from Lagna Pada yogas apply also from 2nd of Lagna Pada
claim: All yogas narrated with reference to the 7th from Lagna Pada (rules 022-025) should also be considered from the 2nd of Lagna Pada. The 2nd from Lagna Pada functions as an additional reference point alongside the 7th.
notes: Meta-rule for engine: apply duplicate evaluation with 2nd from Lagna Pada as the reference house for rules 022-025. The 2nd from Lagna Pada relates to accumulated wealth (Dhana Pada territory).

title: Mercury/Jupiter/Venus (any one) exalted in 2nd from Lagna Pada — rich
claim: If any one of Mercury, Jupiter or Venus is exalted in the 2nd from Lagna Pada and is with strength, the subject will be rich.
notes: The 'with strength' qualifier means the planet must be strong — not just exalted in sign but also powerful overall (Shadbala, Ashtakavarga context). Mercury exaltation = Virgo; Jupiter = Cancer; Venus = Pisces.

title: All Lagna Pada yogas apply from Karakamsa as well
claim: All yogas narrated with reference to Lagna Pada (rules 008-027) should similarly be evaluated from Karakamsa. Karakamsa is the Navamsa occupied by the Atmakaraka (the planet with the highest longitude in the chart). For Karakamsa details see ch.49; for Atmakaraka see ch.32.
notes: This extends the entire Ch29 predictive framework to Karakamsa as a second lagna reference. Engine must support Karakamsa computation from ch.32/49 for these rules to fire.

title: Mercury in 2nd from Arudha Lagna — lord over the whole country
claim: If Mercury is placed in the 2nd from Arudha Lagna (Lagna Pada), the native will lord over the whole country — an extremely high-status outcome.
notes: Mercury in 2nd from Lagna Pada specifically = dominion/sovereignty. This is an elevated king-level yoga. Contrast with rule 030: Venus in 2nd = poet/speaker (artistic, not political power).

title: Venus in 2nd from Lagna Pada — poet or speaker
claim: If Venus is placed in the 2nd from Lagna Pada, the native will become a poet or an eloquent speaker.
notes: Venus in 2nd from Lagna Pada = artistic expression through speech or writing. The 2nd house is the house of speech (Vak Bhava); Venus here through Lagna Pada amplifies that quality.

title: Dara Pada in kendra/trine from Lagna Pada OR both have strong planets — rich and famous
claim: If the Dara Pada (Arudha of 7th house) falls in a kendra (1st, 4th, 7th, 10th) or a trine (1st, 5th, 9th) counted from Lagna Pada, OR if both Lagna Pada and Dara Pada have strong planets, the native will be rich and famous in his country.
notes: Either condition suffices. Dara Pada = 7th bhava Arudha = relates to spouse/partner. Strong mutual positions of Lagna Pada and Dara Pada = overall life prosperity.

title: Dara Pada in 6th/8th/12th from Lagna Pada — poor
claim: If the Dara Pada falls in the 6th, 8th or 12th from Lagna Pada, the native will be poor.
notes: Dusthana placement of Dara Pada relative to Lagna Pada = poverty. Dusthana houses (6/8/12) = houses of loss, obstacles, expenditure.

title: Lagna Pada/7th therefrom, or angle/trine/upachaya from Lagna Pada occupied by strong planet — marital happiness
claim: If the Lagna Pada and the 7th therefrom are occupied by a strong planet, or if an angle (1st/4th/7th/10th), trine (1st/5th/9th), or upachaya (3rd/6th/10th/11th) from Lagna Pada is occupied by a strong planet, there will be happiness between husband and wife.
notes: Marital harmony yoga from Lagna Pada. The upachaya houses (3rd, 6th, 10th, 11th) grow over time — strong planets there indicate improving marital happiness.

title: Lagna Pada and Dara Pada mutually angular or trinal — amity between the couple
claim: If Lagna Pada and Dara Pada are mutually in kendra (angle) or trikona (trine) positions from each other, there will be amity and harmony between husband and wife.
notes: Mutual angular/trinal = strong positive relationship between the spouses. This is one of the key Jaimini marriage compatibility indicators.

title: Lagna Pada and Dara Pada mutually in 6th/8th/12th — mutual enmity in the couple
claim: If Lagna Pada and Dara Pada are mutually in the 6th, 8th or 12th positions from each other, there will doubtlessly be mutual enmity between husband and wife.
notes: Dusthana mutual position of Lagna Pada and Dara Pada = marital conflict or hostility. The text uses 'doubtlessly' (certainly) — flagged as high-strength.

title: Lagna Pada and Dara Pada mutually angular, 3rd-11th, or trinal — king ruling the earth
claim: If Lagna Pada and Dara Pada are mutually in angle (kendra), 3rd-11th axis, or trine (trikona) positions from each other, the native will be a king ruling the earth.
notes: This is the highest status outcome — 'king ruling the earth.' The 3rd-11th axis is added here as an auspicious mutual position (broader than kendra/trikona alone). Tail of Ch29 recovered from Ch30 PDF head.

title: Mutual relationship of Lagna Pada and other Bhava Padas — similar deductions apply
claim: Similar deductions about mutual relationship, gain or loss, kinship dynamics (through son, co-born, wealth etc.) should be made based on Lagna Pada and the relevant Bhava Pada. For example, Lagna Pada and Dhana Pada mutual positions indicate financial relationship dynamics. Lagna Pada and Putra Pada mutual positions indicate progeny relationship.
notes: Meta-rule: the kendra/trine = auspicious, 6th/8th/12th = inauspicious framework for Lagna Pada ↔ Dara Pada applies generally to Lagna Pada ↔ any Bhava Pada. Dhana Pada specifically named in text as example.

title: Condition for gains — 12th from Lagna Pada must be malefic-free
claim: In all cases where gains are indicated through the 11th from Lagna Pada (rules 008-014), the 12th from Lagna Pada must simultaneously be free from malefic association (conjunction or aspect). If malefics afflict the 12th, gains from the 11th are neutralised or reduced. This is a prerequisite condition for the full wealth yogas to manifest.
notes: Explicit prerequisite stated in slokas 13-15 notes. Engine must check 12th from Lagna Pada as a prerequisite before triggering any 11th-from-Lagna-Pada gain rules.

title: Graharudha exceptions — Bhava exceptions do NOT apply to Graharudha
claim: The three special exceptions for Bhavarudha calculation (rules 003-005: same-house rule, 7th-becomes-4th rule, lord-in-4th rule) do NOT apply to Graharudha (planet's Arudha) computation. Graharudha uses the basic formula only — no exceptions.
notes: Explicit in Santhanam's notes on slokas 6-7. Engine must separate Bhavarudha computation (with 3 exceptions) from Graharudha computation (no exceptions).

title: Benefic aspecting 11th from Arudha Lagna from ascendant or 9th — graduated wealth increase
claim: If a benefic placed in the ascendant or the 9th from Lagna Pada aspects the 11th from Arudha Lagna, wealth gains will increase. The aspect from the 9th gives more gains than the aspect from the ascendant — ascending order of benefit.
notes: Graded yoga: benefic in ascendant aspecting 11th from Lagna Pada = good; benefic in 9th from Lagna Pada aspecting 11th from Lagna Pada = better. This is distinct from general benefic aspect on 11th (rule 008) by specifying the planet's own position.

title: 11th Arudha (Labha Pada) aspected by favourable planet — abundant gains
claim: If the Labha Pada (11th Bhava Pada = Arudha of 11th house) is aspected by a favourable planet, there will be abundant financial and professional gains.
notes: Labha Pada = Arudha of 11th house. Aspecting it directly (not 11th from Lagna Pada, but the Labha Pada sign itself) = compounded gain indicator. Example: Jupiter exalted in 9th aspecting both 11th from Arudha Lagna and the Labha Pada itself = abundant gains in Jupiter Dasha.

title: Upa Pada computation — Arudha of 12th house (base BPHS formula)
claim: Upa Pada (Gaunapada) CONFIRMED FORMULA (TT-CH30-01 resolved 2026-05-31): Upa Pada = Arudha of the 12th house (Vyaya Pada). Method: Count how many signs the 12th lord is from the 12th house. Count the same number forward from the lord — that sign is the Upa Pada. Apply standard Arudha exceptions: if result is same house as 12th, use 10th from 12th; if result is 7th from 12th, use 10th from that 7th. IMPORTANT: The parity rule (odd-ascendant→use 12th, even→use 2nd) originates from Chaukamba commentaries and Jaimini variations — it is NOT present in the base BPHS Sanskrit text. Sanskrit verse 2: 'tanoḥ anucarāt yat syāt upārūḍham tat ucyate' — uniformly instructs counting from the 12th house.
notes: TT-CH30-01 ✅ RESOLVED 2026-05-31: Base BPHS formula = Arudha of 12th house. Sanskrit verse 2 unambiguously says to count from the 12th house. The parity rule (odd=12th, even=2nd) is from Chaukamba commentary and Jaimini traditions — valid as an alternate interpretation but NOT the base BPHS instruction. Standard Arudha exceptions from Ch29 slokas 4-5 apply (same-house→10th, 7th→10th from 7th, lord in 4th→4th).
decode_notes: TT-CH30-03 RESOLVED 2026-06-01 via PDF (Ch30 intro notes, pp.303-304). Counting method confirmed: count from the 12th lord's sign (where the 12th lord is placed). Method: (1) find the 12th house, (2) count how many signs the 12th lord is from the 12th house, (3) count the same number of signs forward from the 12th lord's position → gives Upa Pada. Example from Santhanam: Scorpio Lagna, 12th=Libra, lord Venus, count from Libra to Venus position = N signs, then count N from Venus → Upa Pada. NOT counted from the 12th house itself.

title: Upa Pada exceptions — Ch29 exceptions (same-house, 7th, 4th) apply
claim: In calculating Upa Pada, the rules mentioned in Ch29 slokas 4-5 (the three special exceptions for Arudha computation) must be kept in mind: (a) if formula gives same house = use 10th from it; (b) if formula gives 7th from bhava = use 10th from that 7th; (c) if lord is in 4th from bhava = 4th is Arudha. Example from text: Scorpio (odd) ascendant → 12th house is Libra → Venus (Libra lord) is in Cancer → 8 signs from Sagittarius (2nd house from Scorpio — used per even/odd rule for standard nativity where ascendant is Scorpio an odd sign — Santhanam uses 2nd for this example, i.e., even = 2nd).
notes: TT-CH30-01 ✅ RESOLVED 2026-05-31: Standard Arudha exceptions from Ch29 slokas 4-5 confirmed applicable to Upa Pada. Exceptions: (a) if formula gives same house as 12th → use 10th from 12th; (b) if formula gives 7th from 12th → use 10th from that 7th; (c) if 12th lord is in 4th from 12th → 4th is Upa Pada. The Scorpio example ambiguity (even vs odd counting in notes) is now moot — base formula always uses 12th house, so Scorpio (odd or even by various counts) always uses 12th as the reference bhava.

title: Sun — special malefic/benefic classification for Upa Pada context
claim: For Upa Pada evaluations specifically: the Sun is NOT treated as a malefic if he is in exaltation (Aries 10°) or in a friendly sign. The Sun IS a malefic for these purposes if in debilitation (Libra 10°) or in an enemy's sign. This overrides the usual natural malefic classification of the Sun in the context of Upa Pada rules.
notes: Specific to Upa Pada rules only. Does not change Sun's general malefic status in other chapters. Engine must flag Sun's dignity before applying malefic/benefic test in any Ch30 Upa Pada rule.

title: Upa Pada conjunct or aspected by benefic — full happiness from progeny and spouse
claim: If Upa Pada is conjunct or aspected by a benefic planet, the native will obtain full happiness from progeny and spouse.
notes: Benefic aspect/conjunction on Upa Pada = positive outcome for both progeny and spouse. This is the primary Upa Pada auspiciousness indicator.

title: Upa Pada in malefic sign or conjunct/aspected by malefic — ascetic without wife
claim: If Upa Pada is in a malefic's sign OR is aspected by or conjunct a malefic, the native will become an ascetic and go without a wife.
notes: Sun classification is dignity-conditional here per rule 003. Natural malefic signs: Aries, Scorpio (Mars); Capricorn, Aquarius (Saturn); Gemini (partial, Mercury = neutral). The 'ascetic' outcome suggests renunciation of householder life.

title: Upa Pada in malefic sign/aspected by malefic BUT benefic also present — wife not denied
claim: If Upa Pada is in a malefic sign or is afflicted by a malefic BUT there is also a benefic aspect or conjunction on Upa Pada (or on the related malefic), deprivation of spouse will not come to pass — the wife is not denied.
notes: Rescue condition for rule 005. Benefic aspect overrides malefic ascetic combination. Engine must check both malefic and benefic influences before triggering 'no wife' prediction.

title: 2nd from Upa Pada = benefic sign or aspected/conjunct by benefic — same good results for wife and sons
claim: If the 2nd from Upa Pada is a benefic sign or is aspected by or conjunct with a benefic, the same good results as those from Upa Pada itself (happiness from wife and sons) will come to pass.
notes: The 2nd from Upa Pada is the secondary indicator for wife/progeny. If primary (Upa Pada) is afflicted but 2nd is strong, the standard nativity example shows a happily married native.

title: 2nd from Upa Pada has planet in debilitation sign/Navamsa or conjunct debilitated/malefic — destruction of wife
claim: If there is a planet in the 2nd from Upa Pada in debilitation sign or debilitation Navamsa, or conjunct with a debilitated or malefic planet, there will be destruction of wife (early death or divorce).
notes: Notes specify: (a) debilitated planet in 2nd; (b) occupant of 2nd in debilitation Navamsa; (c) benefic joining malefic in 2nd; (d) debilitated benefic in 2nd. All these trigger wife destruction.

title: 2nd from Upa Pada: occupant in exaltation sign/Navamsa or aspected by another — many charming virtuous wives
claim: If the planet occupying the 2nd from Upa Pada is in exaltation sign or exaltation Navamsa, or is aspected by another planet, there will be many charming and virtuous wives.
notes: Multiple virtuous wives — in modern interpretation: second marriage to a worthy partner, or excellent spouse with exceptional qualities.

title: Gemini as 2nd from Upa Pada — many wives
claim: If Gemini happens to be the 2nd from Upa Pada, there will be many wives (plurality of marriage).
notes: Gemini as 2nd from Upa Pada — a sign-specific trigger independent of planetary occupants. Gemini is a dual sign (Dwi-swabhava), which may explain the plurality association. Santhanam's notes also mention Taurus as Upa Pada giving many wives — that belongs in this note for cross-reference.

title: Upa Pada or 2nd from it occupied by own lord, or said lord in other own sign — wife dies at advanced age
claim: If Upa Pada or the 2nd from it is occupied by its own lord, or if the said lord is in his other own house, the wife will die at an advanced age (long life for wife).
notes: Protective combination for wife's longevity even if there are other adverse combinations. The lord in own sign or other own sign is a strong placement that counters early loss of spouse.

title: 7th lord or Venus in own house — loss of wife only at later stage (not early)
claim: If a planet being a constant indicator of wife (7th lord or Venus) is in its own house, there will be loss of wife only at a later stage of life — not early loss.
notes: Protective rule — delays wife loss to later in life. Combined with adverse Upa Pada indicators, this rule mitigates early widowerhood/divorce.

title: Lord of Upa Pada or significator of wife in exaltation — wife from noble family
claim: If the lord of Upa Pada or the constant significator of wife (Venus/7th lord) is in exaltation, the wife will be from a noble family.
notes: Exaltation of Upa Pada lord = wife from noble/aristocratic family. Indicative of status of wife's family, not just personal qualities.

title: Lord of Upa Pada or significator of wife in debilitation — wife from ignoble family
claim: If the lord of Upa Pada or the constant significator of wife is in debilitation, the wife will be from an ignoble/lower family. The reverse of rule 013.
notes: Debilitation of Upa Pada lord = wife's family is of low status. Debilitation: Sun-Libra, Moon-Scorpio, Mars-Cancer, Mercury-Pisces, Jupiter-Capricorn, Venus-Virgo, Saturn-Aries.

title: 2nd from Upa Pada related to a benefic — wife is beautiful, fortunate and virtuous
claim: If the 2nd from Upa Pada is related to (conjunct or aspected by) a benefic planet, the wife will be beautiful, fortunate and virtuous.
notes: Overlaps partially with rule 007 (2nd with benefic = good results for wife and sons). This rule specifically details the wife's qualities: beauty, fortune, and virtue.

title: Saturn + Rahu in 2nd from Upa Pada — loss of wife through calumny or death
claim: If Saturn and Rahu are both in the 2nd from Upa Pada, the native will lose his wife — either through calumny (false accusation/defamation causing separation) or through death.
notes: Two distinct loss mechanisms: calumny (social/reputational separation) or death of spouse. Saturn = longevity/death; Rahu = scandal/calumny.

title: Venus + Ketu in 2nd from Upa Pada — wife has blood disorders and leucorrhoea
claim: If Venus and Ketu are in the 2nd from Upa Pada, the native's wife will be troubled by disorders of blood and leucorrhoea (gynaecological disorders).
notes: Health of spouse indicator from 2nd from Upa Pada. Venus = reproductive system; Ketu = chronic/mysterious ailments. Blood disorders + leucorrhoea = reproductive health issues for wife.

title: Mercury + Ketu in 2nd from Upa Pada — wife has breakage of bones
claim: If Mercury and Ketu are in the 2nd from Upa Pada, the wife of the native will suffer breakage of bones (fractures, skeletal disorders).
notes: Bone-related affliction for wife. Mercury rules nerves and skin; Ketu in combination here manifests as skeletal issues.

title: Rahu + Saturn + Sun in 2nd from Upa Pada — wife has distress of bones
claim: If Rahu, Saturn and the Sun are in the 2nd from Upa Pada, the native's wife will have distress of bones (chronic bone pain, osteoporosis, or bone degeneration).
notes: Saturn = bones/structure; Rahu = chronic issues; Sun = vitality. Together in 2nd from Upa Pada = wife's skeletal system is compromised.

title: Mercury + Rahu in 2nd from Upa Pada — stout-bodied wife
claim: If Mercury and Rahu are in the 2nd from Upa Pada, the native's wife will be stout-bodied (corpulent/heavyset physique).
notes: Physical appearance of spouse indicator. Rahu expands; Mercury in this context relates to body bulk rather than intellect.

title: 2nd from Upa Pada = Mercury's sign + Mars + Saturn occupying — wife has nasal disorders
claim: If the 2nd from Upa Pada is a sign of Mercury (Gemini or Virgo) and is tenanted by both Mars and Saturn, the wife will suffer from nasal disorders.
notes: Sign-conditional: Mercury's signs (Gemini/Virgo) + Mars + Saturn = nasal affliction for wife. Mercury rules respiratory system including nose.
decode_notes: TT-CH30-02 RESOLVED 2026-06-01 via PDF (Ch30 Slokas 20-21, p.307). Nasal disorder requires BOTH: (1) Mars+Saturn occupy the 2nd from Upa Pada, AND (2) that 2nd house must be a Mercury sign (nasal disorder to wife) or a Mars sign (Aries/Scorpio). The sign type qualifier IS explicitly required in the text — NOT Mars+Saturn in Upa Pada sign alone. This rule correctly encodes the Mercury-sign variant; ch30-022 encodes the Mars-sign variant.

title: 2nd from Upa Pada = Mars's sign + Mars + Saturn occupying — wife has nasal disorders
claim: Similarly, if a sign of Mars (Aries or Scorpio) becomes the 2nd from Upa Pada and is occupied by Mars and Saturn, there will be nasal disorders to the wife.
notes: Parallel to rule 021 but with Mars's own signs (Aries/Scorpio) instead of Mercury's. Mars in own sign + Saturn = inflammatory nasal condition.
decode_notes: TT-CH30-02 RESOLVED 2026-06-01 via PDF (Ch30 Slokas 20-21, p.307). Mars-sign variant: 2nd from Upa Pada = Aries or Scorpio (Mars sign) AND Mars+Saturn occupy it → wife suffers nasal disorders. Sign qualifier (Mars sign) explicitly required in text. See also ch30-021 for Mercury-sign variant. Both rules confirmed correct.

title: Jupiter + Saturn in 2nd from Upa Pada — wife has disorders of ears or eyes
claim: If Jupiter and Saturn are in the 2nd from Upa Pada, the native's wife will suffer from disorders of ears or eyes.
notes: Jupiter rules hearing/ears in some systems; Saturn rules chronic conditions; together = chronic ear or eye disorders for wife.

title: Mercury + Mars (not own signs) or Rahu + Jupiter in 2nd from Upa Pada — wife has dental disorders
claim: If Mercury and Mars are in the 2nd from Upa Pada other than their own signs, or if Rahu is with Jupiter in the 2nd from Upa Pada, the native's wife will suffer from dental disorders.
notes: Two distinct combinations both producing dental disorders. 'Not own signs' qualifier for Mercury+Mars: they are weaker and more afflictive when not in own signs. 2nd house = house of mouth/teeth — relevant here.

title: Saturn + Rahu in Saturn's sign as 2nd from Upa Pada — wife has lameness or windy disorders
